item.title: Banking and Securities Operations Technician - specialist in Market Settlement Team, 12-month opportunity
item.description: About the team The Market Settlements Team (MST) team sits within the Central Banking Operations Division and is responsible for the safe, accurate and timely settlement of securities and cash flows arising from activity determined by Foreign Exchange Division (FED) and Sterling Markets Division (SMD). The team settles a wide range of products, including repos, bond trades, swaps and futures related cash movements and reconciliations, alongside cash funding, collateral management and asset servicing activity including coupons and maturities. MST supports activity across the Bank’s own foreign currency reserves and the Exchange Equalisation Account (EEA) managed on behalf of HM Treasury. About the Role As a Technical Specialist, you will provide subject matter expertise across securities settlement, cash funding, asset servicing custody, and selected derivative products. The role combines direct operational involvement with technical expertise, supporting the accurate and efficient processing of securities and cash movements in a highly controlled environment. You will apply technical expertise to resolve non-standard settlement and asset servicing issues, provide advice and guidance on operational matters, and support a strong risk and control environment by identifying and mitigating operational risks in line with established procedures and governance. Alongside business-as-usual responsibilities, the role offers opportunities to support change initiatives and continuous improvement activity that strengthen delivery across the team and the wider Central Banking Operations Directorate. What You’ll Do 1. Specialist Operational Delivery Deliver and maintain the timely and accurate settlement of securities and cash movements, ensuring compliance with industry standards, market conventions and legal deadlines. Apply detailed knowledge of core banking, payment and securities systems (including Openlink, SWIFT Alliance Access, T24, Fedwire, Euroclear and Clearstream) to support effective end‑to‑end processing, issue resolution and control of settlement activity. 2. Technical Leadership & Issue Resolution Investigate and resolve operational and system related issues, working closely with internal teams to ensure timely and effective resolution. Act as an escalation point for complex operational queries and time critical decisions. Provide technical expertise across the team, acting as a point of reference, mentor and support for colleagues. 3. Change, Testing & Continuous Improvement Support the implementation of change initiatives, including requirements, testing and system releases. Identify and drive process improvements to increase automation, resilience and control effectiveness. Promote operational excellence and a culture of continuous improvement. 4. Controls, Risk & Incident Management Maintain strong operational controls across settlements Support incident assessment by providing clear technical insight on root cause, impact, and remediation and lessons learned. 5. Data, MI & Relationship Management Produce and analyse management information to identify trends, support decision making, and evidence control effectiveness. Act as a key point of contact for stakeholders, including Front Office areas, custodians and counterparties Build and maintain effective working relationships, representing the team in internal and external forums. Role requirements To be considered for this role, candidates must meet all the minimum criteria: Minimum Criteria Demonstrable operational experience and strong working knowledge in at least one of the following areas: securities settlements, collateral management, asset servicing, swaps, and/or futures related cash and reconciliation activity. Proven ability to deliver high quality, well controlled outputs within a regulated operational environment. Strong problem-solving capability, including identifying issues, assessing impacts, and proposing practical resolutions. Essential Criteria Well- developed analytical skills, including the ability to interpret data and make sound, evidence-based recommendations. Ability to understand end to end operational impacts of decisions and changes. Effective organisational and workload management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and work accurately under pressure. Ability to adapt to changing information, anticipating risks and opportunities. Strong interpersonal and communications skills, with the ability to engage effectively with internal and external stakeholders at both junior and senior levels. Proficiency with Excel and other Microsoft applications. In addition to the minimum and essential criteria, candidates will typically demonstrate one or more of the following: Desirable Criteria Broader operational exposure across multiple product areas, with working knowledge in two or more of: securities settlements, collateral management, asset servicing, swaps, or futures. Working knowledge of core banking, payments and securities and data systems/applications: Openlink, SAA / SWIFT, T24, EasyWay, Xact, R, Tableau, Python, PowerBI. Experience delivering change initiatives or working on projects within an operational environment. Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve. At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public. We welcome applications from individuals who work flexibly, including job shares and part time working patterns. We've also partnered with external organisations to support us in making adjustments for candidates and employees in the recruitment process where they're needed. From 1st October 2026, we expect all our colleagues to spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office per month. This is to capitalise on the benefits of working together in person across teams, while maintaining the flexibility offered by home working. Subject to that minimum requirement, individuals and managers should work together to find what works best for them and their team. Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme . If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application. Salary and Benefits Information Location: London This role offers an annual salary range in circa. of £39,360 - £44,280 (depending on skills and experience). In addition, we also offer a comprehensive benefits package as detailed below: Currently a non-contributory, career average pension giving you a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80th of your annual salary for every year worked. There is the option to increase your pension (to 1/65th) or decrease (to 1/105th) in exchange for salary through our flexible benefits programme each year. The Bank has the discretion to vary standard accrual rates and dial up and dial down rates at any time and to withdraw dial up and dial down options at any time. A discretionary performance award based on a current award pool. An 8% benefits allowance with the option to take as salary or purchase a wide range of flexible benefits. 26 days’ annual leave with option to buy up to 12 additional days through flexible benefits. Private medical insurance and income protection. National Security Vetting Process Employment in this role will be subject to the National Security Vetting clearance process (and typically can take between 6 to 12 weeks post offer) and the passing of additional Bank security checks in accordance with the Bank policy. Further information regarding the vetting and security clearance requirements for the role will be provided to the successful applicant, and information about how the Bank processes personal data for these purposes, is set out in the Bank's Privacy Notice . The Bank of England welcomes applications from all candidates, but as a UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) approved sponsor, we have a responsibility to comply with the Immigration Rules and guidance. As such, our ability to employ individuals who require sponsorship for immigration purposes is limited. The Bank cannot guarantee that you and / or the role you are applying for will be eligible for sponsorship and that any application made to UKVI will be successful. Eligibility will therefore be considered on a case by case basis. The Application Process Important: Please ensure that you complete the ‘work history’ section and answer ALL the application questions fully. All candidate applications are anonymised to ensure that our hiring managers will not be able to see your personal information, including your CV, when reviewing your application details at the screening stage. It’s therefore really important that you fill out the work history and application form questions, as your answers will form a critical part of the initial selection process. The assessment process will comprise of two stages. This role closes for applications on 01 October 2026. Please apply online, ensuring that you complete your work history and answer ALL the application questions fully and in detail as your application will not be considered if all mandatory questions are not fully completed.

item.title: Data Protection Rights Case Officer
item.description: Data Protection Rights Case Officer Division: Operations - Communications Department: Communications Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £39,100 to £48,800 and London from £41,600 to £51,900 (salary offered will be based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Associate, L8, Corporate Your external recruitment contact is Raimonda via raimonda.stankute@fca.org.uk Your internal recruitment contact is Fizah via fizahfarouk.ibrahim@fca.org.uk Applications must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. About the FCA and team We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth and shaping the future of UK finance services. Information Disclosure Team who sits within Communications are responsible for managing UK GDPR Rights Requests such as subject access requests alongside Freedom of Information Act (FOIA), UK GDPR and other transparency initiatives such as the Environmental Information Regulations and Re-use of Public Sector Information Regulations. The team plays a key role in helping the FCA meet its statutory obligations, supporting our transparency agenda and ensuring compliance with information rights legislation. This role is critical in managing legal, regulatory and reputational risk, as failure to meet statutory deadlines could result in action from the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) and impact confidence in the FCA as a regulator. Role responsibilities This role focuses on handling Data Subject Access Requests and other information rights requests, rather than general data protection compliance activities Handle Subject Access Requests and other information rights requests in line with the UK GDPR, Data Protection Act 2018, FCA policies and procedures, managing a caseload effectively and meeting statutory deadlines Review, assess and prepare information for disclosure, including identifying relevant records, applying appropriate exemptions and carrying out redactions where necessary Liaise with business areas across the FCA to obtain information, provide guidance, build effective working relationships and ensure responses are accurate and delivered on time Draft clear written responses to requesters and other stakeholders, explaining complex information in a straightforward and accessible way Keep up to date with developments in data protection law, ICO guidance and information rights best practice, sharing knowledge, delivering training and raising awareness across the organisation Support evolving team priorities, including Freedom of Information requests and executive correspondence, demonstrating a collaborative and flexible approach Skills required Minimum Experience of handling Data Protection Rights requests, including Data Subject Access Requests, under the UK GDPR and Data Protection Act 2018 Experience of applying legislation, ICO guidance and organisational policies to make sound and defensible decisions Effective written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex issues clearly and accurately to a range of audiences Demonstrated ability to handle several competing tasks and meet deadlines consistently Essential Demonstrated ability to manage a high-volume caseload, consistently meeting statutory and internal deadlines Experience of reviewing large volumes of information and preparing accurate, high-quality disclosures, including the use of redaction software and other disclosure tools Thorough attention to detail and sound judgement when reviewing information, applying exemptions and drafting responses Demonstrated stakeholder management skills, with experience of providing clear, practical advice and working collaboratively across teams, business areas and senior stakeholder groups Demonstrated ability to work with minimal supervision while contributing positively to a collaborative, values-led environment where professionalism, accountability and teamwork lead to successful outcomes SC Clearance is required for this role. You will hold, or be required to obtain, Security Check (SC) level vetting Benefits 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually Colleagues spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office each month (60% for Directors and Executive Directors) across our London, Leeds and Edinburgh offices. A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page . Our values and culture Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation and delivers better regulation. item.description: Job title: Revenue Manager (F TC until Nov 2027) Division: Operations Department: F inance and Corporate Services - Revenue Operations Salary: London from £65,400 to £8 9 , 866 (salary offered will be based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Corporate - Manager Your external recruitment contact is Raimonda via raimonda.stankute@fca.org.uk Your internal recruitment contact is Lauren via Lauren.McHale@fca.org.uk Applications must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. About the FCA and team We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth and shaping the future of UK finance services. The Revenue Operations team delivers the FCA's fee-raising function, managing the modelling, invoicing and collection of regulatory fees and levies to support the organisation's Annual Funding Requirement. Acting on behalf of the FCA and other regulatory bodies, the team maintains the integrity of the regulated population, administers fees and charges, provides specialist stakeholder guidance and supports policy and regulatory developments. In 2025/26, the team was responsible for collecting approximately £2.3bn in fees and levies. Role responsibilities Lead and develop a multi-disciplinary team, building capability and succession planning while supporting continuous improvement, improving controls and reducing operational risk Oversee the end-to-end delivery of the FCA’s fees modelling and invoicing processes, ensuring outputs are accurate, transparent and aligned with approved policy, supported by robust data governance and controls Contribute to the development and implementation of fees policy, providing pragmatic advice on how regulatory change can be effectively translated into operational delivery across systems and processes Oversee financial performance and reporting, including month-end activity, debt management and income tracking, ensuring clear, timely insight is provided to senior stakeholders Build and maintain effective relationships across the FCA and with external regulatory bodies, representing the Revenue function and shaping outcomes in a complex stakeholder environment Provide oversight of key operational processes, ensuring continuity of critical activities and that systems, controls and financial frameworks support efficient, compliant delivery Skills required Minimum Team leadership: Proven experience in leading and developing teams to achieve results while promoting capability and continuous improvement Analytical skills: Strong analytical abilities, with experience in handling large and complex datasets, generating insights, and ensuring data accuracy and integrity Stakeholder engagement: Proficient in managing relationships and communicating effectively with both technical and non-technical audiences in regulated environments Fee structure knowledge: Familiarity with applying fee rules and policies to generate fees effectively Essential Fee policy expertise : In-depth knowledge of fee policies and their practical application in fee generation Leadership and delegation: Ability to lead through challenges, delegate tasks effectively, and maintain accountability within the team Delivery focus: Strong focus on managing priorities, deadlines, and ensuring high-quality outputs that meet governance, risk, and control standards Problem solving: Advanced analytical and problem-solving skills to address complex issues and deliver effective solutions Governance awareness: Experience in applying governance principles and maintaining operational efficiency Benefits 2 8 days annual leave plus bank holidays Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually Colleagues spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office each month (60% for Directors and Executive Directors) across our London, Leeds and Edinburgh offices. item.title: Head of Agentic AI and Data Science Research
item.description: The FCA has retained Global Resourcing to manage this role; send applications directly to Global Resourcing. About the FCA At the FCA, we’re creating a fair and more resilient financial system. We’re establishing more transparent relationships between financial services and customers, building trust in financial markets and protecting vulnerable consumers. We’re currently on an exciting journey as we drive forward significant organisational, people, process, and AI and technology transformation to become a more forward-thinking, proactive regulator. We will use data more effectively to drive better regulatory decisions and build greater cohesion across our broad financial services remit. Significant improvements in digital enablement, business intelligence, market data and information management maturity are all being pursued to maintain our position as a world leader in financial services regulation. In March 2025, the FCA launched a new 5-year strategy to deepen trust, rebalance risk, support growth and improve lives. The FCA will focus on four priorities: Be a smarter regulator; predictable, purposeful and proportionate. The FCA will improve its processes and embrace technology to become more efficient and effective. Support sustained economic growth, by enabling investment, innovation and ensuring the continued competitiveness of the UK’s world-leading financial services. Help consumers navigate their financial lives by working with industry to boost trust, product innovation and ensuring the right information and support is available for people to take financial decisions. Fight financial crime, focusing on those who seek to use the fact they are regulated to do harm. It will go further to disrupt criminals and support firms to be an effective line of defence. The Role The Head of Agentic AI and Data Science Research leads the FCA's capability at the frontier of applied AI, ensuring the organisation not only adopts emerging technologies but understands, shapes and governs them in a way that supports its public interest objectives. Reporting to the Director of Intelligence & Digital, this role is the research and design engine for AI. It provides strategic leadership for AI research, model governance, data science capability, and horizon scanning. It is responsible for identifying how emerging AI technologies can be applied safely, ethically and proportionately to support better regulation, enhance regulatory intelligence, combat financial crime and improve organisational effectiveness. The role owns the FCA's medium and longer-term AI agenda, translating emerging opportunities and risks into actionable strategies, governance frameworks and capability roadmaps. It also leads the FCA Data Science Profession and provides technical thought leadership to senior decision-makers across the organisation and wider regulatory, and technology stakeholder communities. Working closely with AI Product Delivery and AI Security & Technology Operations, the role ensures clear accountability across strategy, research, governance, delivery and operations, without duplication of responsibility. What will the candidate get from the role? Joining the Senior Leadership Team at the FCA during an exciting and challenging time of great change in financial services and its regulation Leading a department of talented and committed people through significant projects whilst also delivering on business-as-usual objectives Exposure to strategic issues and key players in the world of finance, both nationally and internationally Key responsibilities: Lead the FCA's Agentic AI and Data Science Research function, setting the strategic direction for AI research, advanced analytics and emerging technologies Define and shape the FCA's medium and long-term approach to AI and Data Science, ensuring emerging technologies support smarter regulation, regulatory intelligence, financial crime reduction and organisational effectiveness Establish and maintain the FCA's AI governance and research ethics framework, providing the standards, controls and technical authority required for the safe, ethical and proportionate use of AI and advanced analytics Develop and maintain the FCA's medium and long-term AI and Data Science roadmap, translating research, horizon scanning, and emerging technologies into future organisational capability and priorities Lead the FCA's horizon scanning and AI intelligence capability, identifying emerging opportunities and risks, and translating them into strategic recommendations, policy insight and investment priorities Lead the FCA's Data Science Profession; provide specialist AI and Data Science expertise, building professional standards, organisational readiness, and thought leadership while representing the FCA across regulatory, technology, and stakeholder communities Developing and delivering a long-term strategy for the department, aligning to broader divisional and organisational strategies Leading on performance, capability and culture within the department, with a strong focus on operational excellence Delivering through others by relying on coaching, influencing and negotiating skills with a range of internal and external stakeholders Building a strong and inclusive directorate that attracts and develop diverse talent Skills/Experience Required We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer, and therefore, people or individuals with disabilities and long-term conditions who best meet the minimum criteria for a role will go through to the next stage of the recruitment process. In cases of high application volumes we may progress applicants whose experience most closely matches the role’s key requirements. (To learn more about the Disability Confident Scheme Click Here ) Minimum Significant experience of managing and influencing senior stakeholders internally and externally Experience leading specialist technical, analytical, AI, data science or comparable multidisciplinary teams within a complex organisation Strong understanding of AI, machine learning, data science, and advanced analytics, including associated opportunities, limitations and risks Experience of developing governance frameworks, standards, operating models or strategic roadmaps supporting the safe, ethical, and proportionate use of AI or advanced analytics Proven ability to translate complex technological developments into practical organisational outcomes, priorities, and investment decisions Essential Experience developing strategic, tactical, and ethical approaches for deploying AI and advanced analytics in support of organisational objectives Proven horizon-scanning capability and ability to convert emerging technological developments into actionable strategies, and business roadmaps Experience establishing AI governance, model assurance, research ethics or responsible AI frameworks. Ability to operate credibly as a senior technical adviser to executive and board-level stakeholders. Exemplary communication, influencing, and stakeholder management skill Experience of role modelling strong leadership behaviours in line with organisational values The ability to inclusively lead a group of talented individuals with a wide variety of professional expertise, experience, and backgrounds An open and flexible management style and the ability to communicate effectively to a wide-ranging audience with different skills and perspectives Desirable Advanced understanding of agentic AI, multi-agent systems, and emerging frontier AI technologies. Experience within financial services, regulation or another highly regulated environment. Evidence of recognised thought leadership within AI, data science, or advanced analytics. Experience representing an organisation externally on AI strategy, governance, or innovation topics. Familiarity with commercially available agentic AI platforms and tooling. The FCA’s Values & Diversity Our ambition is to create a diverse and inclusive workplace that reflects the society we serve, helping us to be a better regulator. We serve the public and our decisions directly affect the wellbeing of people, businesses and the UK economy. So, our values matter. They represent the culture we aspire to every day, guiding our judgements, building trust and helping us to be ‘At our best’. The FCA is committed to achieving greater diversity across all levels of our organisation. Given this, we particularly welcome applications from women, disabled, and minority ethnic candidates, as under-represented groups. As an inclusive employer, we are open to considering flexible working arrangements, including job shares. Please inform the recruiter if you wish to apply for this role on a flexible basis. As part of the FCA’s on-going commitment to develop our national presence, most of our vacancies are now open to working in our Edinburgh, Leeds or London offices. This means that as part of the application process you will be able to select your preference of which office location you would like to work from. Application Support We want to remove any possible barriers and are committed to providing a wide range of reasonable adjustments so that you can keep the focus on your conversations and be at your best. If you have an accessibility requirement, disability, or condition that means you might require changes to the recruitment process, please contact your recruiter to discuss this further. Our aim is to make you application as easy as possible, and your recruiter will be happy to work with you to make any necessary arrangements where possible. Benefits Our competitive benefits scheme gives you the opportunity to create a personalised benefits package, tailored to suit your lifecycle. You can this this allowance to purchase additional benefits such as dental or cycle to work, or you have the option to top up your base salary by taking this as cash. Core benefits that you will receive as standard are: 30 days holiday per year plus bank holidays Pri

item.title: Technical Specialist - CTP Supervision
item.description: Job Title: Technical Specialist – CTP Supervision Division: Supervision, Policy & Competition (SPC) Department: Market Intervention – Trading Venues Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £74,900 to £88,966 and London £82,300 to £97,800 (salary offered will be based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Technical Specialist – Regulatory Your external recruitment contact is Steve Christopher via steve.christopher@fca.org.uk . Your internal recruitment contact is Katherine Whipps via katherine.whipps@fca.org.uk . Applications must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. About the FCA and team We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth and shaping the future of financial services in the UK. SPC oversees firms and individuals (supervision), creates and reviews the rules by which they operate (policy) and identifies and remedies ineffective competition in markets (competition). The Market Intervention - Trading Venues Department, part of the Infrastructure & Exchanges Directorate, is at the heart of the FCA's work to promote resilient, transparent and fair UK financial markets. The team supervises trading venues, develops policy for trading venues and investment firms operating both on-venue and OTC and delivers early, evidence-based interventions to address emerging risks while contributing to UK and international policy. Within the department, the Trading Policy Team shapes and implements policy across wholesale markets, covering investment exchanges, broker-dealers, proprietary trading firms and commodity derivatives trading firms. Our work spans trading venue requirements, market transparency, algorithmic and high-frequency trading, commodity derivatives and market data. The team is also responsible for the supervision of the bond Consolidated Tape (CT) and leads the development of the regulatory framework for the equity CT, a significant new market infrastructure that will improve the quality, accessibility and transparency of wholesale market data, support price formation and best execution and enhance market integrity across UK financial markets. Role responsibilities Shape the design and lead the delivery of the FCA’s supervisory strategy for the CT, helping improve market transparency, integrity and confidence across UK financial markets Collaborate closely with colleagues across Authorisations, Legal, Trading Policy, Market Oversight and Trading Venue Supervision, building effective partnerships to deliver effective and coordinated regulatory outcomes Lead complex supervisory issues and cases, applying your regulatory knowledge and experience to make informed judgements, provide recommendations and address emerging risks Support, guide and develop team members while helping oversee resources, creating an inclusive, collaborative and high-performing environment Leverage market data, insights and analytics to enhance supervision, build data analytics skills and inform decision-making, improving outcomes for market participants, investors and consumers across the UK Skills required Minimum: Prior experience of financial services and financial regulation Prior experience of representing an organisation externally in a leadership role on technically demanding issues Essential: Thorough understanding of the UK regulatory framework, particularly relating to financial markets, transparency and market data Ability to quickly acquire, source, manipulate and analyse data to inform decision-making Demonstrated ability to evaluate complex issues and make evidence-based judgements, including where information may be incomplete Effective communication skills, with the ability to explain complex issues clearly and succinctly to a range of audiences, including senior stakeholders Clear commitment to collaborative working, with the ability to positively challenge and influence others while providing support and guidance to colleagues Benefits 28 days annual leave plus bank holidays Colleagues spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office each month (60% for Directors and Executive Directors) across our London, Leeds and Edinburgh offices. Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page . Our values and culture Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation and delivers better regulation. If you require any adjustments due to a disability or condition, your recruiter is here to help - reach out for tailored support. We welcome diverse working styles and aim to find flexible solutions that suit both the role and individual needs, including options like part-time and job sharing where applicable. Disability confident: our hiring approach We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer and therefore, people or individuals with disabilities and long-term conditions who best meet the minimum criteria for a role will go through to the next stage of the recruitment process. In cases of high application volumes we may progress applicants whose experience most closely matches the role’s key requirements. Useful information and timelines Timeline: Job advert close: Sunday 27th September at Midnight CV Review/Shortlist: w/c 28th September 2026 1st stage Interviews: w/c 5th and 12th October 2026 2nd stage Interviews: w/c 19th and 26th October 2026 Your Recruiter will discuss the process in detail with you during screening for the role, therefore, please make them aware if you are going to be unavailable for any date during this time

item.title: Application Support Analyst, Audit Technology Services
item.description: Job description Contract type: Permanent Location: London or Newcastle Salary: c.£50,479 (London), c.£42,778 (Newcastle) a higher base may be considered for an exceptional candidate Office attendance: The NAO operates a hybrid working policy where staff are expected to be in the office a minimum 2 days a week. Main purpose of the job: The National Audit Office (NAO) has made a strategic investment in audit technology and automation to enhance audit quality, efficiency, and value for money. This role provides application support for business-critical audit systems, helping to keep services reliable, secure and effective for auditors. The postholder will support day-to-day operations, controlled system change and service improvement. The role helps ensure audit technology supports audit delivery while meeting NAO security, privacy and governance requirements. As an Application Support Analyst, you will support specialist audit applications used by around 700 financial audit users. These are core business systems, not standard helpdesk tools, and the role is focused on maintaining reliable, secure services, supporting controlled change and improving how the applications are supported and used. You will work with NAO colleagues and third-party suppliers to resolve issues, support releases and upgrades, maintain clear documentation and identify improvements from service data, user feedback and recurring incidents. Key responsibilities: • Provide high-quality application support for users, taking ownership of incidents and service requests through to resolution or escalation. • Investigate application issues, identify recurring problems, support root-cause analysis and agree fixes or workarounds with technical teams or suppliers. • Complete business-as-usual administration, including joiner, mover and leaver activity, access changes and periodic access reviews, ensuring least-privilege access and clear audit evidence. • Monitor application availability, performance, capacity, data quality and service trends, using insight to identify risks and recommend improvements. • Support incident, problem, change, release and knowledge management processes, including controlled configuration changes, maintenance and updates. • Plan and complete functional, regression and user acceptance testing for releases, patches and infrastructure changes, including test scripts, evidence, defect management and post-release checks. • Coordinate supplier support tickets, provide clear evidence, monitor service performance and escalate recurring issues or risks as needed. • Create and maintain support procedures, knowledge articles, user guidance, training materials, service reporting and other documentation to support consistent team delivery. • Support the development and delivery of user training or knowledge-sharing activities where this helps improve application use, reduce repeat queries and support effective adoption of changes. • Support projects and the transition of new or changed services into business-as-usual operation, ensuring support, monitoring, documentation, access, resilience and supplier arrangements are ready. • Participate in extended-hours support during peak periods and occasional out-of-hours work for upgrades, maintenance or priority issues. Skills and Experience Essential skills • Experience supporting business-critical applications or digital services, including incident triage, service requests, escalation and resolution. • Good understanding of application support and IT service management, including incident, problem, change, release, deployment and knowledge management. • Ability to diagnose application issues, identify recurring problems and work with technical teams or suppliers to agree fixes or workarounds. • Experience supporting releases, upgrades or patches, including testing, evidence recording and defect management. • Experience creating or supporting user guidance, training materials or knowledge-sharing content to help users understand application changes and common support processes. • Ability to use service data, ticket trends, user feedback and reporting tools to monitor performance, identify risks and support continuous improvement. • Good data and analysis skills, including intermediate Excel skills and the ability to present information clearly for operational reporting and decision-making. • Awareness of access management, information security and data protection, including least-privilege access and clear audit evidence. • Familiarity with ITIL principles or equivalent service management practices Desirable skills • Understanding of Dynamics 365, Microsoft Power Platform and Dataverse would be an advantage, particularly where these support configuration, application administration, data management, workflow automation, integration and service support. • Familiarity with SharePoint, Azure DevOps and SQL. • Awareness of Application Insights and experience of setting up or using performance monitoring would be an advantage, particularly to support service reliability, issue investigation and continuous improvement. • Interest in emerging technologies, including automation and AI, and how these may potentially support audit technology services in the future. Abilities • Delivers high-quality customer service and a positive user experience. • Communicates clearly and effectively with users and stakeholders. • Able to work at pace, prioritise effectively, and manage multiple issues or tasks. • Works confidently with third-party suppliers, escalating issues appropriately. • Collaborates effectively with colleagues across different teams and seniority levels. • Applies logical, solutions-focused thinking to resolve problems. Out of Hours and Peak Period Working During the peak financial audit period (May, June and July), the postholder will be required to participate in an extended hours support rota. Shifts may fall between 8:00am and 7:00pm Monday to Friday, and between 10:00am and 4:00pm on Saturdays and Sundays, allocated fairly across the team via a planned rota. In addition, the postholder may occasionally be required to work out of hours to support system upgrades, planned maintenance or priority issues where service continuity is essential. Where you are required to work extended or out of hours shifts, you will receive overtime payments in line with NAO policy. To apply candidates should provide: -An up-to-date CV -A covering letter of no more than 2 pages clearly demonstrating how you meet the essential criteria and providing relevant examples from your experience The closing date for applications is 23:59 on Monday 28th September Please note that we reserve the right to close this vacancy early if a high volume of applications is received. Selection process Shortlisted candidates will be invited to attend an initial Teams interview during WC 12th of October, followed by panel interview during WC 19th October or 26 October. Nationality Requirements: -UK nationals -nationals of Commonwealth countries who have the right to work in the UK -nationals from the EU, EEA or Switzerland with (or eligible for) status under the European Union Settlement Scheme (EUSS) Please note, we are not able to sponsor work visas. Please contact us at hrservicedesk@nao.org.uk should you have any questions on your nationality eligibility. Equal opportunities and diversity Disability and Reasonable Adjustments: Applicants with a disability who wish their application to be considered under the Disability Confident scheme should confirm this when submitting their application. Under this scheme we guarantee an interview to an applicant with a disability who meets the minimum requirements for the role. You should also let our HR team know if you wish us to consider any Reasonable Adjustments at any stage of the process (HR Service Desk ( HRServiceDesk@nao.org.uk ). We are committed to fair and open recruitment. All applications will be assessed on merit against the requirements of the role. We do not discriminate on the basis of any protected characteristic as defined by the Equality Act 2010.

item.title: Consumer and Wholesale Investment Firms Supervisor
item.description: Job title: Consumer and Wholesale Investment Firms Supervisor Division: Authorisations Department: EHGO (Early & High Growth Oversight) – Consumer and Wholesale Investments Team Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £52,400 to £64,000 and London from £57,700 to £70,000 per annum (salary offered will be based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Senior Associate – Regulatory Your external recruitment contact is Benjamin via benjamin.paulon@fca.org.uk. Your internal recruitment contact is Katie via Katherine.Baker@fca.org.uk Applications must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. About the FCA and Team We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth, and shaping the future of UK finance services. The Early and High Growth Oversight (EHGO) department within the FCA’s Authorisations Directorate supervises firms to raise standards, prevent harm and support growth, focusing on newly authorised and rapidly growing firms. EHGO works across diverse sectors, engaging with start-ups, scaling firms and innovative business models. . As a supervisor in the Consumer and Wholesale Investments team in EHGO, you will proactively supervise firms across the advisers and intermediaries, asset management, wealth management and platforms portfolios, support delivery of key projects, and experience first-hand how EHGO aims to raise standards and improve firm experiences. Role Responsibilities Lead the supervision of firms, managing complex issues to protect consumers and market integrity. Work quickly and collaboratively to tackle harm, assess compliance with relevant rules and requirements, and proactively seek ways to support firms navigate the regulatory landscape and promote growth, Engage constructively with firms through verbal and written communication to influence and support firms effectively. Build effective relationships with colleagues in different areas of the FCA, including Authorisations, Supervision and Enforcement to deliver joined-up, consistent, and proportionate regulatory outcomes. Build and maintain strong regulatory and technical knowledge of the consumer and wholesale investments markets. Play a key role in supporting the delivery of broader departmental and divisional projects. Skills Required Minimum: Experience analysing complex information, making sound risk-based judgements and clearly presenting key issues and recommendations Experience working in financial services and solid technical knowledge of consumer and wholesale investments markets, including associated consumer and market harm Experience building and managing effective relationships with stakeholders at all levels, including senior management and external parties Essential: Experience of managing complex casework and competing priorities to tight deadlines Demonstrable ability to assess, explain and escalate complex risks clearly, even in high-stakes situations Self-motivated and organised, able to take initiative, make timely decisions and respond well to changing demands Skilled at managing stakeholders, building collaborative relationships and steering outcomes Proficient in using data, analytics and visualisation tools to identify trends and deliver actionable insights Professional and well organised, working well with others, and able to manage multiple priorities while contributing to shared outcomes Benefits 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection, and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually Colleagues spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office each month (60% for Directors and Executive Directors) across our London, Leeds and Edinburgh offices A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits, and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page . Our Values and Culture Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference, and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation, and delivers better regulation. If you require any adjustments due to a disability or condition, your recruiter is here to help – reach out for tailored support. We welcome diverse working styles and aim to find flexible solutions that suit both the role and individual needs, including options like part-time and job sharing where applicable. Disability Confident: our hiring approach We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer , and therefore, people or individuals with disabilities and long-term conditions who best meet the minimum criteria for a role will go through to the next stage of the recruitment process. In cases of high application volumes we may progress applicants whose experience most closely matches the role’s key requirements. Useful Information and Timelines Timeline: Job advert closing: 22nd September 2026 (midnight) CV Review/Shortlist: 24th - 25th September 2026 Interviews w/c: 1st - 8th October 2026 Your Recruiter will discuss the process in detail with you during screening for the role, therefore, please make them aware if you are going to be unavailable for any date during this time.

item.title: Junior Developer
item.description: Job description Contract type: Permanent Location: London or Newcastle with a minimum of 2 days per week in the office in line with our hybrid working policy. Salary: London Salary -c£ 45,316; Newcastle: Salary- c£ 38,403 more may be available for exceptional candidates Role overview The National Audit Office (NAO) is the UK’s independent public spending watchdog. We support Parliament in holding government to account and help improve public services through high-quality audit, analysis and insight. Our work is influential, evidence-based and focused on improving value for money for the taxpayer. The NAO welcomes applications from everyone. We value diversity in all its forms and are committed to creating an inclusive culture in which all colleagues can develop and maximise their potential. We support flexible working and are happy to discuss working arrangements with candidates at application stage. Main purpose of the role The Junior Developer will join AI, Data and Analytics Team (AIDA) to help design, build, test and maintain digital tools that support financial audit work across the Financial Audit service line. The role will contribute to the development of business-critical applications, data products and automation that help audit teams work efficiently, consistently and securely. This is a development role for someone with some practical coding experience, typically gained through 1–3 years in a development, data or technical role. The successful candidate will be able to work independently on defined coding tasks, while also collaborating with developers, analysts, testers and audit specialists to turn user needs into reliable, maintainable and well-documented solutions. Main responsibilities -Develop, maintain and improve applications, scripts and tools that support financial audit delivery. -Write clear, reliable and maintainable code, following agreed team standards and good development practice. -Support the development of front-end and back-end components, including user interfaces, APIs and data processing logic. -Work with structured and semi-structured data, helping to prepare, transform, validate and analyse data for use in audit tools. -Assist with testing, quality assurance and defect resolution, including documenting test results and maintaining an audit trail. -Collaborate with colleagues to understand user requirements, translate them into development tasks and deliver outputs to agreed timescales. -Contribute to documentation, user guidance, technical notes and handover materials so that applications can be supported effectively. -Learn new tools, frameworks and development approaches as AIDA’s technology stack evolves. Relationships and Accountability The role will sit within AIDA and report to the development lead within the team. The postholder will work closely with other developers, analysts, testers, audit teams, and colleagues responsible for technology, infrastructure and digital services across the NAO. They will be expected to work collaboratively, raise issues early and contribute to a professional team culture focused on quality, learning and delivery. Essential criteria assessed at application sift -Knowledge of Python and the ability to use it to solve practical development or data problems. -Knowledge of JavaScript and an understanding of how it is used to build interactive user interfaces or web applications. -Understanding of programming fundamentals, such as functions, variables, data structures, control flow, unit testing, integration testing and -debugging. -Ability to work with data and apply basic data quality checks, validation and transformation. -Ability to produce clear, structured and concise written documentation for technical and non-technical audiences. Additional essential criteria -Attention to detail and a commitment to developing reliable, secure and maintainable solutions. -Ability to work collaboratively, respond constructively to feedback and contribute as part of a multidisciplinary team. -Interest in the work of the NAO and in using technology, data and evidence to improve public services. Desired criteria -Knowledge of SQL and experience querying relational databases. -Knowledge of R, including experience using R for analysis, reporting or application development. -Knowledge of DevOps practices and Agile methodology, including how multidisciplinary teams plan, deliver and improve software products iteratively. -Knowledge of Git and version control, including branching, committing, reviewing and managing code changes collaboratively. -Knowledge of how containerisation supports the development, testing and deployment of reliable applications across different environments. -Knowledge of cloud platforms and data services, such as Azure, Google Cloud Platform or AWS. -Knowledge of CI/CD practices and how automated build, test and deployment pipelines support reliable software delivery. -Awareness of web application frameworks, APIs or client-server application design. -Awareness of testing approaches, code review, accessibility, security or deployment processes. -Awareness of WCAG accessibility requirements and how to implement solutions within apps. -Awareness of how artificial intelligence and automation can be used responsibly to support analysis, software development and audit work. Attributes -Intellectual curiosity and a willingness to learn new technologies and development approaches. -Inclusive and collaborative in approach, with a commitment to treating colleagues with respect, valuing different perspectives and helping create a team environment where everyone can contribute. -Problem-solving mindset, with the confidence to investigate issues and ask for support when needed. -Commitment to high-quality work, including careful documentation and a reliable audit trail. -Flexibility to contribute across different projects, users and technical challenges. -Professional judgement, including awareness of confidentiality, data protection and the importance of secure development. -Drive and determination to overcome obstacles and deliver useful, practical outcomes. What the role offers This role offers the opportunity to contribute to work that matters from the start. The postholder will help build tools used by audit teams across the NAO, learn from experienced developers and analysts, and develop skills in software engineering, data, testing and public sector audit technology. The role will provide exposure to a range of projects, from maintaining existing applications to supporting new tools and approaches as AIDA’s technical capabilities evolve. To apply candidates should provide: -An up-to-date CV -A covering letter of no more than 2 pages clearly demonstrating how you meet the essential criteria and providing relevant examples from your experience The closing date for applications is 23:59 on Sunday 4 October Please note that we reserve the right to close this vacancy early if a high volume of applications is received. Selection process Shortlisted candidates will be invited to assessment and interview starting WC 19 October Nationality Requirements: -UK nationals -nationals of Commonwealth countries who have the right to work in the UK -nationals from the EU, EEA or Switzerland with (or eligible for) status under the European Union Settlement Scheme (EUSS) Please note, we are not able to sponsor work visas. Please contact us at hrservicedesk@nao.org.uk should you have any questions on your nationality eligibility. Equal opportunities and diversity Disability and Reasonable Adjustments: Applicants with a disability who wish their application to be considered under the Disability Confident scheme should confirm this when submitting their application. Under this scheme we guarantee an interview to an applicant with a disability who meets the minimum requirements for the role. You should also let our HR team know if you wish us to consider any Reasonable Adjustments at any stage of the process (HR Service Desk ( HRServiceDesk@nao.org.uk ). We are committed to fair and open recruitment. All applications will be assessed on merit against the requirements of the role. item.title: Senior Manager, Data & Statistics in REGULATORY DATA GROUP
item.description: Senior Manager, Data & Statistics in the Regulatory Data Group Location: Leeds The Data and Statistics Division (DSD) is the Bank’s centre of expertise for the collection, compilation, dissemination, and publication of regulatory and statistical data. As part of this, DSD encourages innovation and promotes quality to support analysis, policy and decision-making by the Bank’s various committees, as well as UK government departments and international organisations. DSD collects data from banks and buildings societies, credit unions, insurance companies, regulated mortgage lenders and mortgage administrators. This is done via nearly 40 statistical collections and over 200 regulatory collections. We cleanse a sizeable proportion of these datasets and publish a large volume of statistical data via our interactive database. We support the Bank’s policy committees and the Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA) Board. Our data are used in a number of publications, such as the Monetary Policy Report, Financial Stability Report, Credit Conditions Survey, Stress Test Results, FPC Core Indicators, and Quarterly Bulletins. Job description The Division is seeking to appoint a Senior Manager to lead its Regulatory Data Group (RDG). The RDG Senior Manager will work closely with the DSD Leadership Team to support the division’s strategic direction. This is an exciting period of change for DSD, leading and feeding into multiple Data Transformation Programmes and delivery of the Bank wide Data and Analytics Strategy. As regulatory data stewards for the PRA, RDG employs advanced analytics and machine learning techniques to ensure high standards of data quality are maintained and continuously enhanced. This is essential for continued integrity and effectiveness of our regulatory framework. The successful candidate will be responsible for ensuring that RDG is strategically positioned, appropriately structured, and equipped with the capabilities required, ensuring regulatory data services evolve to support future operating models, technologies and business requirements to meet the evolving challenges and priorities of the Bank. The Senior Manager will set the strategic direction for the group, drive delivery of key outcomes, and provide constructive challenge to support informed decision-making and continuous improvement. They will act as a credible and inclusive role model for a diverse and highly skilled team, investing in the development, wellbeing, and success of colleagues to maximise individual and collective performance. As a senior leader within both DSD and DAT, the job holder will play a key role in shaping the future direction of the Division and Directorate, contributing actively to leadership discussions, organisational development, and strategic decision-making to ensure RDG, DSD and DAT remain well positioned to meet future business needs. Key Responsibilities • Lead the Regulatory Data Group (RDG), ensuring it delivers its core objective of regulatory data stewardship for the PRA while maintaining the right organisational structure, skills, capacity and capabilities to meet the Bank's future needs. • Manage senior relationships with key PRA stakeholders and represent DSD in senior governance forums for Regulatory Data collection. • Ensure RDG is appropriately structured and resourced, with clear accountabilities, succession plans and capability development pathways that enable effective delivery of current priorities and future strategic objectives. • Review and adapt the Group's operating model, ways of working and resource allocation to ensure RDG remains resilient, efficient and fit for purpose. • Manage RDG's budget effectively and work collaboratively with Senior Manager peers to optimise the use of resources across the Division. • Support and champion the delivery of DAT and DSD strategies, ensuring RDG contributes fully to wider Directorate priorities, projects and transformation initiatives. • Provide strategic leadership and constructive challenge, fostering a culture of continuous improvement, collaboration and innovation. Minimum Criteria: • Demonstrated ability to lead and shape teams with varied work portfolios, ensuring the right mix of skills, expertise and resources to deliver high-quality outcomes against demanding deadlines. • Experience of building and maintaining strong relationships with a wide range of stakeholders, including senior leaders, to influence outcomes and deliver strategic objectives. • Strong interpersonal and communication skills, both written and verbal, with the ability to represent the Division and Directorate effectively at senior levels and with external organisations. • Experience of leading teams through periods of change, including adapting structures, priorities and resources to meet changing business requirements. • Knowledge of data governance, data quality management or data stewardship frameworks. Essential Criteria: • Strong people leadership and line management skills, including experience of building, developing and organising teams to meet current and future business needs. • Experience of workforce planning, organisational design or capability development, ensuring teams have the right structure, skills and capacity to deliver effectively. • Experience of leading staff with significant domain expertise while fostering collaboration, professional development and continuous improvement. • Strong strategic thinking, problem-solving and planning skills, with the ability to align team structures and priorities to wider organisational objectives. • Experience of influencing both internal and external stakeholders and driving change across organisational boundaries. • Excellent written and oral communication skills, including the ability to communicate complex issues clearly to a range of audiences. Desirable Criteria: • Understanding of regulatory reporting frameworks, prudential regulation, supervisory data, or broader financial sector data requirements. Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve. At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public. We welcome applications from individuals who work flexibly, including job shares and part time working patterns. We've also partnered with external organisations to support us in making adjustments for candidates and employees in the recruitment process where they're needed. From 1st October 2026, we expect all our colleagues to spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office per month. This is to capitalise on the benefits of working together in person across teams, while maintaining the flexibility offered by home working. Subject to that minimum requirement, individuals and managers should work together to find what works best for them and their team. Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme . If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application. Salary and Benefits Information We encourage flexible working, part time working and job share arrangements. Part time salary and benefits will be on a pro-rated basis as appropriate. This role offers a salary of £83,440 - £93,870 per annum (depending on skills and experience). In addition, we also offer a comprehensive benefits package as detailed below: Currently a non-contributory, career average pension giving you a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80th of your annual salary for every year worked. There is the option to increase your pension (to 1/65th) or decrease (to 1/105th) in exchange for salary through our flexible benefits programme each year. The Bank has the discretion to vary standard accrual rates and dial up and dial down rates at any time and to withdraw dial up and dial down options at any time. A discretionary performance award based on a current award pool. An 8% benefits allowance with the option to take as salary or purchase a wide range of flexible benefits. 26 days’ annual leave with option to buy up to 12 additional days through flexible benefits. Private medical insurance and income protection. National Security Vetting Process Employment in this role will be subject to the National Security Vetting clearance process (and typically can take between 6 to 12 weeks post offer) and the passing of additional Bank security checks in accordance with the Bank policy. Further information regarding the vetting and security clearance requirements for the role will be provided to the successful applicant, and information about how the Bank processes personal data for these purposes, is set out in the Bank's Privacy Notice . The Bank of England welcomes applications from all candidates, but as a UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) approved sponsor, we have a responsibility to comply with the Immigration Rules and guidance. As such, our ability to employ individuals who require sponsorship for immigration purposes is limited. The Bank cannot guarantee that you and / or the role you are applying for will be eligible for sponsorship and that any application made to UKVI will be successful. Eligibility will therefore be considered on a case by case basis. The Application Process Important: Please ensure that you complete the ‘work history’ sect

item.title: Data Scientist in the Cross Firm Team (CFT) - ARTIS
item.description: LEEDS BASED The ARTIS Directorate The Authorisations, Regulatory Technology and International Supervision (ARTIS) Directorate brings together the PRA’s Authorisations Division, the RegTech, Data and Innovation Division, and four divisions supervising UK activities of internationally headquartered banks, custodians and designated investment firms. It provides global leadership through data analytics, technical capability, consistent supervision and regulatory transactions, working collaboratively across the PRA and wider Bank. The Cross Firm Team (CFT) The CFT provides cross-firm financial analysis, risk identification, and thematic reviews across the international banking section. Combining supervisory insight with cutting-edge analytics, the team supports supervisors, seniors, and the wider Bank in identifying emerging risks, understanding industry trends, and taking informed supervisory action. The ARTIS Data Science Spoke (ADSS) ADSS is a team of dedicated data scientists within the CFT developing innovative artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and advanced analytics capabilities to deliver more effective and efficient use of data within ARTIS and ultimately drive better decision making. Job Description The role holder will sit at the intersection of AI implementation and supervision and lead contributions to the development of advanced analytics capabilities. They will interface with data scientists, supervisors, and technical experts to ensure that ADSS is best serving the data needs of ARTIS. As a result, they will gain insight into how international banks operate, and are supervised, as well as sitting at the forefront of AI implementation in the PRA. A key part of ADSS’ ongoing workplan is to maximise opportunities opened by the PRA’s future data product, Supervisory Analytics and Metrics (SAM). SAM sits on the Enterprise Data Platform (EDP), and the role holder will play a leading role in assessing and implementing cloud-based AI solutions, including pipelines and products spanning Azure Data Factory and Databricks which include state-of-the-art AI & ML techniques. Number of direct reports: 0 Role Responsibilities Lead the design and development of cutting-edge AI tools and products to make better use of supervisory data. Work with supervisors and technical specialists to understand analytics gaps and design the innovative future data landscape within ARTIS to meet them. Lead contributions to strategic Bankwide and PRA initiatives such as the Enterprise Data Platform (EDP) and Supervisory Analytics and Metrics (SAM). Keep abreast of frontier AI developments to constantly assess and explore new opportunities to innovate alongside other PRA data scientists. Build and maintain strong collaborative relationships with key partners at all levels. This may include representing ADSS in presentations to senior committees. Role Requirements Minimum Criteria: Experience contributing to projects that apply AI or ML techniques to drive more effective and efficient use of data. Experience developing data pipelines using best practices in data engineering, AI, and ML. Ability and willingness to proactively seek out opportunities to innovate. Essential Criteria: Keen interest in learning how investment banks operate, how international banks are supervised, and general banking business models. Proficiency in Python and/or R, or their Spark equivalents. Excellent stakeholder management skills, and the ability to communicate technical concepts to non-technical audiences. Strong problem-solving skills, and the ability to deliver under pressure. Ability and willingness to stay updated on frontier AI developments. Desirable Criteria: Experience working with solutions that involve Large Language Models (LLMs) and agentic approaches, including evaluating the efficacy of them. Experience working with Databricks and/or Azure Data Factory or other cloud-based tools and technologies. Experience working with PowerBI and/or JavaScript for the purpose of front-end development. Familiarity with MLOps and LLMOps frameworks such as MLFLow for the purposes of development and maintenance of AI solutions in a cloud environment. Experience developing and deploying Streamlit and Shiny content on a Posit Connect server. Pre-existing knowledge of how investment banks operate, how international banks are supervised, and general banking business models. We know that candidates do not always apply if they do not fully meet every criterion. We are most interested in an innovative mindset and technical potential. If this role excites you and you can bring an analytical skillset that you think would fit, we encourage you to apply or reach out to discuss the role. Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve. At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public. We welcome applications from individuals who work flexibly, including job shares and part time working patterns. We've also partnered with external organisations to support us in making adjustments for candidates and employees in the recruitment process where they're needed. From 1st October 2026, we expect all our colleagues to spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office per month. This is to capitalise on the benefits of working together in person across teams, while maintaining the flexibility offered by home working. Subject to that minimum requirement, individuals and managers should work together to find what works best for them and their team. Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme . If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application. Salary and Benefits Information We encourage flexible working, part time working and job share arrangements. Part time salary and benefits will be on a pro-rated basis as appropriate. Salary is circa £51,360 - £57,000. In addition, we also offer a comprehensive benefits package as detailed below: Currently a non-contributory, career average pension giving you a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80th of your annual salary for every year worked. There is the option to increase your pension (to 1/65th) or decrease (to 1/105th) in exchange for salary through our flexible benefits programme each year. The Bank has the discretion to vary standard accrual rates and dial up and dial down rates at any time and to withdraw dial up and dial down options at any time. A discretionary performance award based on a current award pool. An 8% benefits allowance with the option to take as salary or purchase a wide range of flexible benefits. 26 days’ annual leave with option to buy up to 12 additional days through flexible benefits. Private medical insurance and income protection. National Security Vetting Process Employment in this role will be subject to the National Security Vetting clearance process (and typically can take between 6 to 12 weeks post offer) and the passing of additional Bank security checks in accordance with the Bank policy. Further information regarding the vetting and security clearance requirements for the role will be provided to the successful applicant, and information about how the Bank processes personal data for these purposes, is set out in the Bank's Privacy Notice . The Bank of England welcomes applications from all candidates, but as a UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) approved sponsor, we have a responsibility to comply with the Immigration Rules and guidance. As such, our ability to employ individuals who require sponsorship for immigration purposes is limited. The Bank cannot guarantee that you and / or the role you are applying for will be eligible for sponsorship and that any application made to UKVI will be successful. Eligibility will therefore be considered on a case by case basis. The Application Process Important: Please ensure that you complete the ‘work history’ section and answer ALL the application questions fully. All candidate applications are anonymised to ensure that our hiring managers will not be able to see your personal information, including your CV, when reviewing your application details at the screening stage. It’s therefore really important that you fill out the work history and application form questions, as your answers will form a critical part of the initial selection process. The assessment process will comprise of two interview stages. This role closes on 12th October. Please apply online, ensuring that you complete your work history and answer ALL the application questions fully and in detail as your application will not be considered if all mandatory questions are not fully completed.
