item.title: Personal Assistant to the Head of Department
item.description: Job Title: Personal Assistant to the Head of Department Division: Authorisations Department : Banking & Insurance and Early & High Growth Oversight Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £28,800 to £38,000 and London from £31,600 to £42,000 (salary offered will be based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Senior Professional Support - Corporate Your internal recruitment contact is Katie via katherine.baker@fca.org.uk Your external recruitment contact is Riley Fox via riley.fox@fca.org.uk . Applications must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. About the FCA and team We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth, and shaping the future of UK finance services. The Authorisations Division serves as the initial point of contact for firms and individuals seeking to provide regulated financial services in the UK, making authorisation decisions to ensure applicants meet the FCA’s standards. We are looking for an experienced PA to support the Head of Department of our Banking & Insurance and Early & High Growth Oversight Department in Authorisations. The department has two functions – Banking & Insurance Authorisations deals with applications for new banks, insurers, funeral plan providers and insurance intermediaries, and Early & High Growth Oversight supervises firms in the early stages of being regulated and when experiencing high growth. Role responsibilities Providing a dedicated and professional service to the HoD, assembling and disseminating information on their behalf and progressing actions as appropriate Monitoring of emails, including the recording and tracking of actions Diary management – ensuring commitments are managed smoothly, within time constraints, and that associated arrangements (e.g. briefing requests) operate efficiently Manage meeting papers for the HoD including coordinating briefings, managing bring forward/pending system and chasing 'actions' from others where necessary Preparing agendas for the Management meetings and following up actions where necessary Acting as a point of contact for the HoD, including liaison with senior management and external stakeholders Investigating issues and resolving queries (escalating/advising HoD as appropriate) and ensuring full communication with contacts/Division as relevant Coordinating departmental communications and any other ad hoc papers or presentations Skills required Minimum: Experience working in a Personal Assistant capacity with well-developed organisational skills Experience of establishing and maintaining effective relationships with senior stakeholders Experience using Microsoft Outlook, OneNote, Excel, Word and PowerPoint Essential: Ability to work professionally in demanding situations with tight deadlines and to balance competing priorities Ability to make timely decisions based on relevant analysis in absence of the HoD where appropriate Ability to work on own initiative and manage time effectively Ability to work effectively with a range of internal and external stakeholders Collaborative worker with the ability to work on own initiative Committed to improving processes and sharing good practice The role requires you to have access to sensitive and confidential information. Maintaining security and confidentiality of information is of paramount importance in this role Benefits 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays Colleagues spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office each month (60% for Directors and Executive Directors) across our London, Leeds and Edinburgh offices Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection, and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits, and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page . Our values & culture Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference, and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation, and delivers better regulation. If you require any adjustments due to a disability or condition, your recruiter is here to help - reach out for tailored support. We welcome diverse working styles and aim to find flexible solutions that suit both the role and individual needs, including options like part-time and job sharing where applicable. Disability Confident: our hiring approach We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer , and therefore, people or individuals with disabilities and long-term conditions who best meet the minimum criteria for a role will go through to the next stage of the recruitment process. In cases of high application volumes, we may progress applicants whose experience most closely matches the role’s key requirements. Useful information and timeline Advert Closing: 30th September 2026 CV Review/Shortlist: 2nd - 6th October 2026 Interviews: w/c 12th October 2026 Your Recruiter will discuss the process in detail with you during screening for the role, therefore, please make them aware if you are going to be unavailable for any date during this time.

item.title: Listings Corporate Finance Senior Specialist
item.description: Job title: Listings Corporate Finance Senior Specialist Division: Enforcement & Market Oversight Department: Listings Salary: London ranging from £59,200 to £76,800 and National (Edinburgh & Leeds) ranging from £53,800 to £69,600 (salary offered will be based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Senior Associate – Regulatory Your recruitment contact is Riley at riley.fox@fca.org.uk - Applications must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. About the FCA and team We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth, and shaping the future of UK finance services. Enforcement & Market Oversight (EMO) is responsible for the FCA’s responsibilities for market monitoring, delivery of the functions of the UK Listing Authority (UKLA) and the investigation and prosecution of misconduct using the whole spectrum of criminal, civil and administrative sanctions and remedies against firms and individuals. The Listings Department sits within the Market Oversight Directorate (MO) at the Financial Conduct Authority. The Department has a key role in the regulation of capital markets activity in the UK. We are currently recruiting a Senior Associate to join our Listings Department. The role offers an excellent opportunity to gain a sound and practical working knowledge of primary markets regulation along with in depth exposure to the transactions making the headlines in the business pages, including major IPOs, equity capital raises such as rights issues, Mergers and Acquisitions (M&A) activity and non-equity issuances including structured products, sukuks, high yield bonds and medium term note programmes. You will also develop project management and influencing skills, take on significant levels of responsibility and deal with a variety of advisers on technical issues. As your career develops there may be opportunities to work with other areas within the FCA in ad hoc cross-cutting teams. You will have a rare opportunity to be involved in the workings of the FCA as capital markets regulator at a time of considerable change. You will enjoy a unique insight into the full spectrum of capital markets activity, with the opportunity to have a real impact whilst working collaboratively towards a common goal alongside a range of internal and external stakeholders. Role Responsibilities You will work in small case teams assigned to review draft prospectuses and circulars, assess eligibility of companies for listing on the London market and respond to written queries on the interpretation of the regime in a novel and complex area Within a case team, you will act as a principle point of contact with the advisory firms who submit cases to the Listings Department for review and will be responsible for preparing comments on the documents provided by companies and their advisers, managing transaction timetables, and liaising with companies’ advisors The work is market-facing, highly time critical, and can require challenging judgments to be made often in pressurised circumstances Skills required Minimum Demonstrable experience of the wider capital markets and/or the corporate transactions carried out by listed companies Proven experience of managing stakeholders Essential Good attention to detail and strong analytical and verbal reasoning skills Excellent communications skills, including written English A motivated approach with the ability to work under pressure and manage a large workload whilst maintaining focus and high standards Highly effective influencing skills, including delivering difficult messages, and a positive attitude to dealing with external parties with a commitment to building effective relationships A team player with the ability to work independently when required The ability to be flexible and adaptable in your approach to encompass new ways of working as required Strong organisational skills with the proven ability to prioritise work and escalate issues The ability to digest a large amount of written information and identify relevant issues from such information Wider experience of capital markets, for example, equity capital markets (ECM) and/or debt capital markets (DCM), knowledge of closed and open-ended investment fund structures and asset management or the broader European capital markets regulatory framework Benefits 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays Colleagues spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office each month (60% for Directors and Executive Directors) across our London, Leeds and Edinburgh offices Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection, and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits, and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page . Our values and culture Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference, and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation, and delivers better regulation. If you require any adjustments due to a disability or condition, your recruiter is here to help - reach out for tailored support. We welcome diverse working styles and aim to find flexible solutions that suit both the role and individual needs, including options like part-time and job sharing where applicable. Disability confident: our hiring approach We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer , and therefore, people or individuals with disabilities and long-term conditions who best meet the minimum criteria for a role will go through to the next stage of the recruitment process. In cases of high application volumes, we may progress applicants whose experience most closely matches the role’s key requirements. Useful information and timelines Timeline: Job advert closing: 27th September at 11:59pm CV Review/Shortlist: 2nd October First Interview: w/c 12th October Your Recruiter will discuss the process in detail with you during screening for the role, therefore, please make them aware if you are going to be unavailable for any date during this time. SC Clearance is required for this role ( SC Guidance ) - you will hold or will be required to obtain Security Check (SC) level vetting

item.title: Professional Training Advisor
item.description: Job description Job title: Learning & Development - Professional Training Advisor Contract type: Permanent Location: London with a minimum of 2 days per week in the office Salary: London c£32,517 per annum plus civil service pension scheme employer contribution of 28.9% Role overview The National Audit Office (NAO) supports Parliament in holding government to account and improving public services, with a focus on driving long‑term, sustainable performance. As an independent body, we scrutinise public spending to ensure value for money for taxpayers and deliver recommendations that lead to financial savings and better service delivery across the public sector. An opportunity has arisen within the Professional Training team (PTT), and the main purpose of this role is to co-ordinate the different stages of the NAO graduate and apprentice programme, supporting onboarding and the qualification pathway of successful students and delivering strong administrative and advisory support across a range of People processes and areas. The successful candidate will provide relevant advice and support to key internal and external stakeholders in an effective and timely way to achieve high service standards. This post will impact successful delivery of a range of Professional Training tasks and will, therefore, affect the contribution of the wider People Team to the business, customer satisfaction and our performance. Key responsibilities The Learning & Development - Professional Training Advisor will be responsible for delivering Professional Training process and assignments in a prompt, accurate and responsive way to a high standard to meet business needs. This will include: -Supporting all administrative aspects of the ACA programme, such as booking study and exam leave, overseeing and reporting on college attendance and mock completion, processing exam results, and supporting payroll inputs. -Working with colleagues to develop study pathways in line with the NAO’s college timetable. -Providing guidance and support throughout the trainee and apprentices qualification journey. -Working collaboratively within the People team to ensure consistency of service, including providing responses to professional training queries received via the HR Portal in a professional manner and to agreed SLAs, escalating complex issues when required. -Supporting communication and engagement with trainees, keeping internal training pages up to date and dealing with qualification queries, escalating to the Senior Professional Training Advisor or Head of Professional Training where required. This will range from dealing with basic queries about college allocations to sensitive and confidential cases impacting their studies. -Build relationships and liaise with external providers, including our college and institute, to ensure a high level of service is provided to the NAO and that they are keeping abreast of new information or issues that may affect the NAO’s work. -Input data accurately and provide management information using NAO’s systems. Undertake data analysis where required (for example exam pass rate analysis). -Monitor and report on ICAEW regulatory activities to key stakeholders. -Priorities and plan work demands and commitments to ensure an efficient service across the wider People team and to deliver work delegated by the Head of Professional Training and Senior Professional Training Advisor. -Follow policy and processes related to their work package accurately, to identify and implement improvements and efficiencies. -Support our People Deal and goals for diversity and inclusion by championing initiatives. -Complete ad-hoc assignments to a high standard Relationships and Accountability Reporting to the Head of Professional Training, you will work closely with graduates and apprentices, performance coaches, and colleagues across the People Team, Finance, and wider corporate services. You will also build strong relationships with external training providers, including colleges and the ICAEW, to ensure a high-quality service. While the role has no direct line or budget management responsibility, you will operate within agreed Professional Training budgets and collaborate with stakeholders at all levels, including senior management, to deliver an effective and responsive service. Essential criteria (used for shortlisting) -Experience in professional qualifications training and/or Learning & Development, ideally within the professional services, education sector or a training provider -Proven administrative and coordination experience in a fast-paced environment -High level of attention to detail and accuracy in data management -Clear and effective communication and presentation skills -Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including data analysis and reporting Key skills and behaviours -Demonstrated knowledge of Professional Qualification Training, Apprenticeships and Learning & Development. -Ability to plan, organise and administer a busy programme of work to a high standard of accuracy and quality, responding to changes in priorities as required, to ensure that key deadlines are met, e.g., exam data processes, monthly pay runs. -High level of attention to detail, working methodically and accurately to ensure all relevant college, student data details are correct. -Self-starter, using creativity and initiative when seeking solutions. -Communication and presentation skills to deliver challenging messages sensitively -The ability to engage and build relationships with internal and external stakeholders -Ability to work well in a team, adopting a collaborative and inclusive approach -Numerical and Microsoft Excel skills, with an ability to analyse data, produce reports and provide accurate management information, in a clear and user-friendly way. -Commitment and motivation to deliver a high-quality service and proactively seeking ways to implement improvements to processes. What we offer -35 days annual leave, including public holidays -Choice of Principal Civil Service Pension Scheme (PCSPS) or a stakeholder pension scheme Flexible working opportunities -Personal and career development support -On-site canteen and gym -Interest-free season ticket loan -Cycle to Work scheme -Online staff discount scheme -Payment of professional subscriptions, health checks and eyesight tests -Enhanced non-contributory death-in-service benefit How to apply Please upload your most recent CV and a Covering Letter no more than 2 pages clearly outlining your interest and suitability for the role against essential criteria and key skills before the deadline. The closing date for applications is 23:59pm Sunday 4 October Selection Process Applicants shortlisted for interview will be asked to complete an Excel assessment in advance. Interviews will take place in person at our offices in Victoria, London during week commencing 19 October Equal opportunities and diversity Disability and Reasonable Adjustments: Applicants with a disability who wish their application to be considered under the Disability Confident scheme should confirm this when submitting their application. Under this scheme we guarantee an interview to an applicant with a disability who meets the minimum requirements for the role. You should also let our HR team know if you wish us to consider any Reasonable Adjustments at any stage of the process (HR Service Desk: HRServiceDesk@nao.org.uk ). Nationality Requirements • UK nationals • Nationals of Commonwealth countries who have the right to work in the UK • Nationals from the EU, EEA or Switzerland with (or eligible for) status under the European Union Settlement Scheme (EUSS) Please note, we are not able to sponsor work visas. Please contact us at hrservicedesk@nao.org.uk should you have any questions on your nationality eligibility.

item.title: Press Officer
item.description: Job description Job Title: Press Officer Contract type: Permanent Location: London with a minimum of 2 days per week in the office in line with our hybrid working policy. Salary: London Salary -c£42,262 pro rata per annum (more may be available for exceptional candidates + Civil Service Pension) Role overview : The National Audit Office (NAO) supports Parliament in holding government to account and improving public services, with a focus on driving long‑term, sustainable performance. As an independent body, we scrutinise public spending to ensure value for money for taxpayers and deliver recommendations that lead to financial savings and better service delivery across the public sector. We are seeking a skilled and proactive Press Officer to join our Press Team. This role is responsible for publicising the work of the NAO to the media to protect and enhance our reputation. The post-holder will need to be able to understand complex, technical information and turn this into simple and engaging messages for our audiences. They will need to be capable of managing proactive, planned press work but have the ability to react to events and enquiries as well. They should also be digitally aware and experienced at using a range of communication tools and channels. Main responsibilities : -Promoting the work of the NAO to external audiences via traditional and social media: -Write press notices, pitches to journalists, op-eds and blog posts promoting our value-for-money and financial audit reports; -Draft social media posts to promote our outputs, working alongside the design team to develop content for multimedia posts; -Brief journalists across print and broadcast on NAO reports to help secure in-depth, accurate and positive media coverage; -Organise and oversee press briefings and media interviews; -Engage with stakeholders, including Parliament, government departments and audited bodies’ press offices; -Support audit teams and NAO spokespeople to communicate our work externally; -Develop communications plans which help achieve audit teams’ impact and influence objectives with our key stakeholders; -Help prepare spokespeople for media interviews by conducting practice interviews and developing support materials; -Respond to time-sensitive, high-profile enquiries from journalists accurately, by drafting reactive lines to take and briefing NAO spokespeople and the media to protect the NAO’s reputation; -Respond appropriately to questions and comments on social media about our work; -Build relationships with national, local and trade press journalists across all sectors our work covers; -Participate in an out-of-hours press office rota with other team members. -Working with press team colleagues to help deliver a range of tasks, including: -Supporting the senior press officers in compiling and sharing media coverage; -Assisting in delivering internal media training for colleagues; -Maintaining media databases compliantly; -Compiling internal reporting statistics. Essential criteria assessed at application sift: -Demonstrable knowledge of the UK media landscape, including a strong news sense and awareness of the UK political environment -Demonstrable writing skills, with the ability to produce clear, accurate, and effective written communications within agreed timescales -Demonstrable communication skills, including the ability to build and maintain effective working relationships with a range of stakeholders and convey messages to different audiences using appropriate communication techniques -Additional essential criteria -The successful candidate should also be able to demonstrate the following: -Ability to translate complex and sensitive information and data into simple language -Experience using digital and print media and able to learn new tools quickly -Able to work under pressure and respond to issues at short notice and out of hours -Effective team player with a demonstrated understanding of other communications disciplines -Proficiency in traditional and social media monitoring -Experience working as a journalist, or in a press office or communications team Desired criteria: -Interest in and understanding of how government works To apply candidates should provide: -An up-to-date CV -A covering letter of no more than 2 pages of A4 clearly demonstrating how you meet the essential criteria and providing relevant examples from your experience The closing date for applications is 23:59 on Sunday 4th October Selection process : Shortlisted candidates will be invited to attend an interview, either in person or online during week commencing 19th October. They will be required to complete an assessment exercise in advance, which will then be discussed during the interview. Nationality Requirements: -UK nationals -Nationals of Commonwealth countries who have the right to work in the UK -Nationals from the EU, EEA or Switzerland with (or eligible for) status under the European Union Settlement Scheme (EUSS) Please note, we are not able to sponsor work visas. Please contact us at hrservicedesk@nao.org.uk should you have any questions on your nationality eligibility. Equal opportunities and diversity : Disability and Reasonable Adjustments: Applicants with a disability who wish their application to be considered under the Disability Confident scheme should confirm this when submitting their application. Under this scheme we guarantee an interview to an applicant with a disability who meets the minimum requirements for the role. You should also let our HR team know if you wish us to consider any Reasonable Adjustments at any stage of the process (HR Service Desk ( HRServiceDesk@nao.org.uk ). We are committed to fair and open recruitment. All applications will be assessed on merit against the requirements of the role. We do not discriminate on the basis of any protected characteristic as defined by the Equality Act 2010.

item.title: Manager, Compliance in PRIVACY (6-month FTC/Secondment)
item.description: Location: Leeds 6 Month FTC Risk Directorate The Bank of England is a diverse organisation. Each of its 4,000 plus people are committed to public Risk management in its broadest sense is at the core of the Bank’s mission and is central to everything we do. As well as the diverse policy risks managed by the Bank’s three policymaking committees, the Bank is also exposed to a wide array of financial and non-financial risks. The Risk Directorate was created following the 2018 internal Risk Governance Review and houses the second line of defence risk and compliance functions charged with providing effective oversight of the Bank’s financial and non-financial risks and ensuring compliance with its policies. The Directorate brought together various second line functions – Bankwide Risk, Financial Risk & Resilience, and the Bank’s central Compliance Division, including Privacy. The Risk Directorate also includes Business Continuity Management. Internal Audit forms the third line of Defence for the bank and is part of the Risk Directorate for administration purposes but operates independently. Department Overview The Compliance Division sits within the Risk Directorate. Risk management in its broadest sense is at the core of the Bank’s mission and is central to everything we do. The Bank’s reputation for integrity and impartiality are key to maintaining our ability to discharge our mission. The Compliance Division is a second line independent oversight function, responsible for reinforcing a culture of compliance across the Bank. The Division The Compliance Division: maintains a bank of clear, accessible and sensible policies, overseeing the quality and consistency and enforcing adherence to appropriate governance; acts to increase staff understanding of the Bank’s key policies and controls, designing a training programme to address key compliance risks / breaches / lack of understanding; fosters an environment of integrity and ethics and acts as a guardian of the Bank’s reputation; ensures that key policy-linked controls are effective and efficient; and, ensures that breaches are appropriately and consistently managed. The Privacy team is part of the Compliance Division and is led by the Bank’s Head of Privacy and Data Protection Officer. The Privacy team owns the Bank’s privacy framework and shares accountability with business areas to ensure that the Bank appropriately manages privacy risk. This includes ensuring compliance with data protection legislation and enabling the efficient and compliant use of personal data held by the Bank. Job Description Reporting to the Bank’s Data Protection Officer and working closely with other Privacy Managers, this is a key role working across the organisation to enable the compliant use of personal data in support of business objectives. The Deputy Data Protection Officer supports the Bank’s Data Protection Officer by providing professional advice and support to the organisation and contributing to strategy development to ensure that privacy compliance supports the Bank’s wider organisational goals. Core responsibilities include: Applying expert knowledge to provide high-quality and timely advice on compliance with all aspects of the Data Protection Act 2018, the UK General Data Protection Regulation, and related legislation, often in relation to complex matters requiring significant analysis; Leading on the completion of Data Protection Impact Assessments and other privacy risk assessments to assess and explain the impact of proposed changes to business processes and agree appropriate mitigating actions with the Risk Owners; Where required, providing advice on the management and resolution of incidents involving personal data, including advising on decisions as to whether to notify regulatory authorities; Preparing and drafting reports on privacy risks and compliance for senior management; Additional responsibilities include: Supporting the Bank’s Data Protection Officer with the management of the Privacy function by leading complex privacy initiatives and workstreams to align with organisational priorities and strategic objectives, developing workplans, managing absences and distribution of work; Supporting the Bank’s Data Protection Officer to carry out statutory obligations including the monitoring of the organisation’s compliance with data protection law and managing individual rights’ requests and complaints; Deputising for the Bank’s Data Protection Officer in the event of absence or unavailability. Number of direct reports: 0 Role Requirements: Minimum Criteria Demonstrable depth and breadth of privacy expertise gained through roles as a privacy practitioner in large or complex organisations; Completion of relevant professional qualifications e.g. CIPP/E, CIPM, CIPT; Experience of carrying out Data Protection Impact Assessments. Essential criteria Ability to work to tight deadlines and respond to competing priorities in a fast paced environment, staying calm under pressure; Proven ability to analyse complex problems; Be able to work autonomously, exercising sound, risk based judgement and critical thinking in relation to privacy risk; Be able to understand broader perspectives whilst retaining an eye for detail; Excellent verbal and written communication skills, able to explain technical matters to stakeholders in a way that is meaningful to the audience. Desirable Criteria Ability to build internal relationships and networks based on credibility, respect and trust. Strong business focus with the ability to work closely with and influence senior management and key decision makers, with the confidence to challenge, negotiate and persuade where appropriate. Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve. At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public. We welcome applications from individuals who work flexibly, including job shares and part time working patterns. We've also partnered with external organisations to support us in making adjustments for candidates and employees in the recruitment process where they're needed. From 1st October 2026, we expect all our colleagues to spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office per month. This is to capitalise on the benefits of working together in person across teams, while maintaining the flexibility offered by home working. Subject to that minimum requirement, individuals and managers should work together to find what works best for them and their team. Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme . If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application. Salary and Benefits Information We encourage flexible working, part time working and job share arrangements. Part time salary and benefits will be on a pro-rated basis as appropriate. The salary range on offer is £62,480 - £70,920. In addition, we also offer a comprehensive benefits package as detailed below: Currently a non-contributory, career average pension giving you a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80th of your annual salary for every year worked. There is the option to increase your pension (to 1/65th) or decrease (to 1/105th) in exchange for salary through our flexible benefits programme each year. The Bank has the discretion to vary standard accrual rates and dial up and dial down rates at any time and to withdraw dial up and dial down options at any time. A discretionary performance award based on a current award pool. An 8% benefits allowance with the option to take as salary or purchase a wide range of flexible benefits. 26 days’ annual leave with option to buy up to 12 additional days through flexible benefits. Private medical insurance and income protection. National Security Vetting Process Employment in this role will be subject to the National Security Vetting clearance process (and typically can take between 6 to 12 weeks post offer) and the passing of additional Bank security checks in accordance with the Bank policy. Further information regarding the vetting and security clearance requirements for the role will be provided to the successful applicant, and information about how the Bank processes personal data for these purposes, is set out in the Bank's Privacy Notice . The Bank of England welcomes applications from all candidates, but as a UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) approved sponsor, we have a responsibility to comply with the Immigration Rules and guidance. As such, our ability to employ individuals who require sponsorship for immigration purposes is limited. The Bank cannot guarantee that you and / or the role you are applying for will be eligible for sponsorship and that any application made to UKVI will be successful. Eligibility will therefore be considered on a case by case basis. item.title: Technical Specialist, Supervision in Operational Resilience Hub
item.description: LEEDS BASED UKDT Directorate The UK Deposit Takers (UKDT) Directorate is responsible for the supervision of over 600 UK banks, building societies and credit unions. Its aim is to contribute to a safe, sound and competitive UK banking system through delivering effective prudential supervision. The Operational Risk & Resilience (ORR) Hub is one of the specialist teams within UKDT Specialist Supervision Division, supporting the supervision of operational risk and resilience across UKDT non-systemic firms. The work we do is varied and wide-ranging, including leading cross-firm thematic and firm-specific reviews, and supporting the PRA’s response to operational incidents at firms. We also work closely with colleagues in SRS and the other Directorates across PRA/ FMID on ORR related risks. Job Description The Technical Specialist – Cyber Risk, provides specialist expertise predominantly on cyber risk, but is also expected to support on operational resilience, technology and third-party risk related work across UKDT non-systemic firms. The role supports supervisory teams through firm assessments, thematic reviews, incident response activity and technical advice, helping ensure firms can prevent, respond to and recover from operational disruptions. The role also contributes to the development of supervisory approaches, supports engagement with senior stakeholders at firms. Key Responsibilities Lead cyber risk and operational resilience reviews of regulated firms. Provide technical support and advice to supervisory teams. Support the PRA's response to significant cyber and operational incidents. Lead or contribute to cross-firm thematic reviews and horizontal work. Assess firms' cyber and operational resilience capabilities, outsourcing arrangements and third-party dependencies. Produce high-quality supervisory assessments, reports and recommendations. Engage with senior stakeholders within firms and across the Bank. Coach and develop colleagues, may include line management responsibilities. Role Requirements Minimum Criteria Experience in cyber security, technology risk, operational resilience, operational risk, audit or a related discipline. Experience assessing or managing technology and cyber risks within a regulated environment. Experience conducting reviews, audits, assurance work or risk assessments. Strong analytical skills and the ability to produce clear written reports and recommendations. Ability to communicate complex technical issues to non-technical stakeholders. Essential Criteria Strong knowledge of cyber resilience, technology risk and operational resilience frameworks. Knowledge of PRA operational resilience, incident reporting and material third-party/outsourcing policy. Understanding of technology outsourcing and third-party risk management. Ability to identify key risks, root causes and supervisory implications. Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills. Experience leading workstreams, projects or supervisory reviews. Ability to manage competing priorities and deliver high-quality outcomes. Strong verbal and written communication skills. Experience coaching, mentoring or developing others. Desirable Criteria Knowledge of technology governance, risk and controls frameworks and standards, such as COBIT, ITIL and ISO 27001. One or more related IT risk qualifications, relevant educational background or equivalent risk management work experience. Knowledge of cloud technology and emerging technology risks. You should not be put off applying if you do not meet all these criteria – we would encourage you to get in touch to discuss if needed. The successful candidate will report to the Senior Technical Specialist. Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. From 1st October 2026, we expect all our colleagues to spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office per month. This is to capitalise on the benefits of working together in person across teams, while maintaining the flexibility offered by home working. Subject to that minimum requirement, individuals and managers should work together to find what works best for them and their team. Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme . If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application. Salary and Benefits Information We encourage flexible working, part time working and job share arrangements. Part time salary and benefits will be on a pro-rated basis as appropriate. Salary is circa £65,440 - £73,000. In addition, we also offer a comprehensive benefits package as detailed below: Currently a non-contributory, career average pension giving you a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80th of your annual salary for every year worked. There is the option to increase your pension (to 1/65th) or decrease (to 1/105th) in exchange for salary through our flexible benefits programme each year. An 8% benefits allowance with the option to take as salary or purchase a wide range of flexible benefits. 26 days’ annual leave with option to buy up to 12 additional days through flexible benefits. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth and shaping the future of financial services in the UK. SPC oversees firms and individuals (supervision), creates and reviews the rules by which they operate (policy) and identifies and remedies ineffective competition in markets (competition). The Payments Policy Team is a large and growing team focused on working closely with HMT Treasury, and colleagues across FCA and PSR, to modernise the payments regulatory framework. This includes work realise the benefits of agentic payments, whilst maintaining a safe and trusted payments system Role responsibilities Lead policy work on agentic payments by shaping proposals, future of payments policy Provide specialist insight by delivering advice and briefings on payments policy issues to colleagues and senior management, shaping FCA strategy Grow your skills by developing deep knowledge of payments services and regulations and the risks and opportunities of agentic AI and agentic payments Be part of transformation by playing a key role in a major regulatory change project, working as a team to develop innovative solutions in an evolving policy landscape Skills required Minimum: Prior experience of analysing information and contributing to the development of policy relating to financial services and/or innovative technology Prior experience of presenting key issues clearly and succinctly, both verbally and in writing Prior experience of building and managing effective relationships with a range of stakeholders Essential: Experience developing policy that supports consumer protection, drives innovation and competition, and/or promotes growth and UK competitiveness Effective problem-solving and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver high-quality outcomes in a fast-paced environment A flexible and proactive approach, demonstrating a willingness to learn, take on new responsibilities, and adapt to changing priorities Benefits 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays Colleagues spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office each month (60% for Directors and Executive Directors) across our London, Leeds and Edinburgh offices. Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page . We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation and delivers better regulation. If you require any adjustments due to a disability or condition, your recruiter is here to help - reach out for tailored support. We welcome diverse working styles and aim to find flexible solutions that suit both the role and individual needs, including options like part-time and job sharing where applicable. Disability confident: our hiring approach We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer and therefore, people or individuals with disabilities and long-term conditions who best meet the minimum criteria for a role will go through to the next stage of the recruitment process. item.title: Digital Reviewer – FTC Until July 2027
item.description: Job title: Digital Reviewer – FTC Until July 2027 Division: Enforcement & Market Oversight Directorate: Enforcement Intelligence and Specialist Services Department: Digital Services, Learning & Business Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £32,500 - £42,000 and London ranging from £35,600 - £45,000 This role is graded as: Associate – Level 9 – Regulatory Your external recruitment contact is: Riley at riley.fox@fca.org.uk Your internal recruitment contact is: Pat at patrycja.matachowska@fca.org.uk Applications must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. About the FCA and team We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth, and shaping the future of UK finance services. Enforcement & Market Oversight (EMO) is responsible for the FCA’s responsibilities for market monitoring, delivery of the functions of the UK Listing Authority (UKLA) and the investigation and prosecution of misconduct using the whole spectrum of criminal, civil and administrative sanctions and remedies against firms and individuals. The Central Digital Review Unit (CDRU) is a specialist team within Enforcement Intelligence and Specialist Services (EISS). We support Enforcement and Market Oversight (EMO) investigations by providing digital evidence review, disclosure support and specialist eDiscovery services, including e-Discovery techniques in the processing, review, and production of evidence. CDRU supports investigation teams by reviewing large, complex and evolving collections of digital material using the eDiscovery Tool (EDT). As eDiscovery and AI technologies continue to develop, CDRU helps teams use these capabilities effectively and responsibly while maintaining robust standards of evidence review, disclosure and quality assurance. Role Responsibilities Review and assess digital material for relevance, evidential value, disclosure issues, privilege, and confidentiality across criminal, regulatory, civil, and dual-track investigations. Work with investigation teams to understand case objectives and recommend proportionate and defensible approaches to eDiscovery and document review. Apply sound judgement to large and complex data sets, identifying material issues, inconsistencies, review risks and matters requiring escalation. Advise and support case teams in the effective use of the EDT. Skills Required Minimum: Practical experience of investigations, litigation, evidence review or disclosure work within a regulatory, criminal, civil, serious fraud or complex financial crime environment. Demonstrable experience of assessing volumes of evidential material in a regulatory, criminal, civil, serious fraud or complex financial crime environment, in accordance with the Criminal Procedure and Investigations Act 1996 (CPIA), preferably using an eDiscovery platform. You currently hold Security Clearance (SC) level vetting Essential: The ability to assess large and complex collections of digital evidence accurately, applying sound judgement and recognising issues that require further consideration or escalation. Capable of organising and prioritising allocated work, maintaining accurate records and delivering high-quality outputs to agreed timescales. A working knowledge of disclosure principles and the Criminal Procedure and Investigations Act 1996. Effective stakeholder skills, including the ability to understand different perspectives, explain complex review issues clearly and provide constructive, evidence-based advice. Able to work with minimal supervision while collaborating effectively with investigation teams, legal colleagues, technical specialists, and other stakeholders Effective written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to record review decisions and methodologies clearly and defensibly. Confidence in learning and using digital systems, with the ability to adapt to evolving eDiscovery, analytical and AI-enabled technologies. Benefits 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection, and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually Colleagues spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office each month (60% for Directors and Executive Directors) across our London, Leeds and Edinburgh offices A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits, and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page . Our Values and Culture Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference, and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation, and delivers better regulation. If you require any adjustments due to a disability or condition, your recruiter is here to help - reach out for tailored support. We welcome diverse working styles and aim to find flexible solutions that suit both the role and individual needs, including options like part-time and job sharing where applicable. Disability Confident: Our Hiring Approach We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer , and therefore, people or individuals with disabilities and long-term conditions who best meet the minimum criteria for a role will go through to the next stage of the recruitment process. In cases of high application volumes, we may progress applicants whose experience most closely matches the role’s key requirements. Useful Information and Timelines Timeline: Job advert closing: 27th September at 11:59pm CV Review/Shortlist: 29 September First Interview: w/c 5th October Your Recruiter will discuss the process in detail with you during screening for the role, therefore, please make them aware if you are going to be unavailable for any date during this time. SC Clearance is required for this role ( SC Guidance ) - you will currently hold Security Check (SC) level vetting

item.title: Product Owner - Graph Analytics
item.description: Job title: Product Owner - Graph Analytics Division: Data, Technology & Innovation (DTI) Department: Digital Intelligence Solutions Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £60,700 to £87,400 and London from £66,600 to £96,300 (salary offered will be based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Lead Associate - Regulatory Your Internal recruitment contact is Pat at Patrycja.matachowska@fca.org.uk . Your external recruitment contact is Ben via benjamin.paulon@fca.org.uk . Applications must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. About the FCA and team We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth, and shaping the future of UK finance services. The Data, Technology and Innovation (DTI) division enables the FCA to be a digital-first, data-led smart regulator by delivering a secure, agile, and cost-effective technology and data ecosystem that drives better decisions, transparency, and operational efficiency. Sitting within DTI, the Digital Intelligence Solutions team deliver a Digital Unified Intelligence Environment (DUIE) to surface insights for action through tools, dashboards and bespoke analysis. Role responsibilities: You will lead the vision, strategy and performance of a complex graph analytics product spanning connected data, analytical services, application programming interfaces and user-facing tools with minimal supervision Own and communicate the product vision, strategy and outcome-based roadmap, balancing user needs, regulatory outcomes, technical opportunities, risk, cost and the FCA’s strategic objectives Lead the full product lifecycle, from discovery and validation through development, operation, continuous improvement and retirement, using evidence to decide when to invest, continue, change direction, pause or stop Apply solid technical understanding of graph analytics to shape product choices, review architecture and analytical proposals, and identify where graph approaches will and will not add value, while working with technical leads who retain detailed engineering and architecture accountability Lead prioritisation and planning across a core multidisciplinary team and dependent platform and engineering teams, managing scope, uncertainty, dependencies and delivery risk Use research, data and direct engagement to understand user problems, test assumptions and turn needs into prioritised outcomes. Build consensus with regulatory users, technical specialists and senior stakeholders Own product performance, adoption, benefits, budget, operating cost, risk and lifecycle decisions. Define success measures, report transparently and use qualitative and quantitative evidence to enable continuous improvement Skills required: Minimum: Demonstrated experience leading a complex digital, data, or technology product across multiple lifecycle stages, including setting strategy, prioritizing an outcomes-focused roadmap, and delivering through multidisciplinary teams Prior experience managing technically complex data or analytical products Demonstrable experience using graph analytics and graph technologies, including graph data models, databases and query languages Essential: Solid product management practice, including strategic ownership, user-centred discovery, outcome-based roadmapping, prioritisation under uncertainty and evidence-based lifecycle decisions Experience leading a multidisciplinary product team and coordinating delivery through dependent platform and engineering teams, while maintaining clear accountability for product outcomes rather than acting primarily as a delivery manager Ability to engage credibly with engineers, data scientists and architects on data models, architecture, scalability, performance, data quality, explainability, technical debt and operational resilience Experience applying user-centred, Agile and Lean approaches pragmatically, using research, service data and feedback to validate priorities, measure outcomes and improve the product Commercial and value-for-money judgement, including ownership of product budgets and operating costs, and balancing investment, user value, organisational benefit and risk Experience owning the ongoing performance of a live data or analytical product, including adoption, service performance, risk, governance, security, privacy, auditability and human oversight Benefits: 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays Colleagues spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office each month (60% for Directors and Executive Directors) across our London, Leeds and Edinburgh offices Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection, and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits, and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page . Our Values & Culture Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference, and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation, and delivers better regulation. If you require any adjustments due to a disability or condition, your recruiter is here to help - reach out for tailored support. We welcome diverse working styles and aim to find flexible solutions that suit both the role and individual needs, including options like part-time and job sharing where applicable. In cases of high application volumes we may progress applicants whose experience most closely matches the role’s key requirements. item.title: 12 month FTC PA in ECONOMIC OUTLOOK DIVISION & CURRENT ECONOMICS DIVISION
item.description: Location: Leeds and London Directorate / Division Overview Monetary Policy Assessment and Strategy provides the core analytical support that helps the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) make decisions on monetary policy to meet the inflation target. The area brings together expertise in economic analysis, forecasting and policy strategy, working closely with colleagues across the Bank and the MPC Unit. Within the area, the Economic Outlook and Current Economic Conditions divisions play a central role in assessing developments in the UK and global economy, producing analysis that supports the MPC's understanding of inflationary pressures and the outlook for growth and inflation. We are seeking a highly motivated, organised and proactive Personal Assistant to provide high-quality support to the Head of Divisions and selected senior managers. This is a varied and interesting role in a dynamic area of the Bank, offering exposure to senior stakeholders, divisional management activity and cross-Bank work. The jobholder will provide a full secretarial, administrative and operational support service. They will be expected to manage competing priorities, exercise sound judgement, build strong relationships across the Bank and handle sensitive information with discretion. The role would suit someone who enjoys working at pace, takes pride in delivering excellent support and is keen to improve processes and ways of working. The successful candidate will be part of a wider PA and support team. The team is self-covering, so the jobholder will be expected to work flexibly with other PAs, provide cover during absences and contribute positively to the wider support community, including cover for more senior PA offices where required. You would: Provide proactive, high-quality PA support to the Head of Divisions and selected senior managers, acting as a trusted point of contact and using judgement when handling requests. Manage complex and frequently changing diaries, resolve scheduling conflicts, prioritise competing meeting requests and ensure senior leaders have sufficient preparation time. Proactively manage inboxes, monitor correspondence, highlight urgent matters, coordinate responses and ensure actions are progressed promptly. Organise divisional management meetings, leadership meetings and wider staff events, including agendas, papers, minutes and action tracking. Work with the Head of Divisions and management teams to keep the divisions running effectively, highlighting outstanding actions, chasing deadlines and supporting governance activity. Build and maintain strong working relationships with colleagues at all levels, including senior internal stakeholders and external contacts. Support recruitment activity, including arranging interviews, preparing interview packs, coordinating candidate communications and supporting onboarding arrangements. Complete joiner, mover and leaver processes and help ensure colleagues have a positive experience when joining or moving within the division. Arrange domestic and international travel, prepare itineraries, process expenses and support budget tracking or other administrative processes through the year. Identify opportunities to improve, streamline or automate divisional processes, including making effective use of Microsoft 365 tools and new technologies. Work collaboratively with the wider PA network, providing cover across divisions and supporting senior PA offices when required. There is some flexibility to shape the role around the successful candidate’s strengths and interests, particularly in relation to process improvement, divisional coordination and wider PA community contribution. Role Requirements: Minimum Criteria This role requires strong PA or executive support experience, excellent judgement and the ability to provide calm, proactive support in a busy senior leadership environment. ​​ You should have:​ Strong organisational, prioritisation and time management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines. Experience managing complex diaries, inboxes, meetings, papers, actions, travel and expenses. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with confidence engaging with colleagues at all levels. Sound judgement, discretion and professionalism when handling sensitive or confidential information. A proactive, self-starting approach, with the ability to work independently, use initiative and solve problems. Flexibility, resilience and the ability to remain calm and effective under pressure. Proficiency in Microsoft Office and Microsoft 365 tools, particularly Outlook, Word, PowerPoint, Teams, OneNote and Excel. Essential Criteria A collaborative approach and commitment to inclusive, respectful working practices. Excellent attention to detail and commitment to delivering accurate, high-quality work. Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to build effective relationships and networks quickly. Desirable Criteria Experience of having supported Heads of Divisions or Department level or above. Taking minutes of meetings Basic MS Excel skills. Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve. At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public. We welcome applications from individuals who work flexibly, including job shares and part time working patterns. We've also partnered with external organisations to support us in making adjustments for candidates and employees in the recruitment process where they're needed. From 1st October 2026, we expect all our colleagues to spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office per month. This is to capitalise on the benefits of working together in person across teams, while maintaining the flexibility offered by home working. Subject to that minimum requirement, individuals and managers should work together to find what works best for them and their team. Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme . If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application. Salary and Benefits Information We encourage flexible working, part time working and job share arrangements. Part time salary and benefits will be on a pro-rated basis as appropriate. The salary for this role is, Leeds: £25,760 - £28,980 and London: £28,640 - £32,220 In addition, we also offer a comprehensive benefits package as detailed below: Currently a non-contributory, career average pension giving you a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80th of your annual salary for every year worked. There is the option to increase your pension (to 1/65th) or decrease (to 1/105th) in exchange for salary through our flexible benefits programme each year. The Bank has the discretion to vary standard accrual rates and dial up and dial down rates at any time and to withdraw dial up and dial down options at any time. A discretionary performance award based on a current award pool. An 8% benefits allowance with the option to take as salary or purchase a wide range of flexible benefits. 26 days’ annual leave with option to buy up to 12 additional days through flexible benefits. Private medical insurance and income protection. National Security Vetting Process Employment in this role will be subject to the National Security Vetting clearance process (and typically can take between 6 to 12 weeks post offer) and the passing of additional Bank security checks in accordance with the Bank policy. Further information regarding the vetting and security clearance requirements for the role will be provided to the successful applicant, and information about how the Bank processes personal data for these purposes, is set out in the Bank's Privacy Notice . The Bank of England welcomes applications from all candidates, but as a UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) approved sponsor, we have a responsibility to comply with the Immigration Rules and guidance. As such, our ability to employ individuals who require sponsorship for immigration purposes is limited. The Bank cannot guarantee that you and / or the role you are applying for will be eligible for sponsorship and that any application made to UKVI will be successful. Eligibility will therefore be considered on a case by case basis. The Application Process Important: Please ensure that you complete the ‘work history’ section and answer ALL the application questions fully. All candidate applications are anonymised to ensure that our hiring managers will not be able to see your personal information, including your CV, when reviewing your application details at the screening stage. It’s therefore really important that you fill out the work history and application form questions, as your answers will form a critical part of the initial selection process. The assessment process will comprise of two interview stages. (Amend and add brief details if relevant, such as interview/assessment dates or process for your specific role) This role closes on 5th October 2026 Please apply online, ensuring that you complete your work history and answer ALL the application questions fully and in detail as your application will not be considered if all mandatory questions are not fully completed.

item.title: Appointment of Members to the Northern Ireland Fiscal Council
item.description: NORTHERN IRELAND FISCAL COUNCIL BRINGING GREATER TRANSPARENCY AND INDEPENDENT SCRUTINY TO THE CURRENT AND FUTURE CONDITION OF NORTHERN IRELAND’S PUBLIC FINANCES. Appointment of Members The Department of Finance is seeking to appoint up to three new members for the Northern Ireland Fiscal Council. The terms of appointment will be for five years. The aim of the Council is to bring greater transparency and independent scrutiny to the current and future state of Northern Ireland’s public finances, to inform public debate, and policy decisions. It provides independent reporting on the Executive’s performance in delivering its budget. Members are appointed by the Finance Minister for their independence and expertise, and are expected to act impartially, free from political influence. They should be willing and able to engage with Assembly Committees, contribute to public discussion, and speak at events on matters relating to public finances. The appointments come at an exciting time for the Council which having been formed in 2021, has recently gone through the Assembly process to place it on a statutory footing. Members of the Council will require a commitment of up to 30 days per annum to the appointment. This position will be paid at a rate of £390 per day. The appointment is non-pensionable. How to Apply For more detailed information on the role and person specification, please click on the 'Candidate Information Booklet' link below. In order to apply for this position, please click on the 'Apply for this job online' link below to register to this vacancy and to submit an online application. Alternatively you can request an application pack by contacting: HRConnect, PO Box 1089, Beacon House, 27 Clarendon Road Belfast BT1 9EX. Telephone: 0800 1 300 330. Email: recruitment@hrconnect.nigov.net All requests must include your name, address and reference number IRC330471. The application pack can also be requested in alternative formats by contacting HRConnect. Reasonable adjustments will be made to accommodate the needs of those with a disability. Completed application forms must be returned to arrive not later than 12:00 noon (UK time) on Friday 9th October 2026. Applicants invited for interview are eligible for reimbursement of reasonable travelling expenses incurred within Europe. It is anticipated that interviews will be held in Colby House, Stranmillis Court, Stranmills Road, Belfast BT1 9RR on 14 and 15 December 2026. Equality of Opportunity : The Department is committed to the principle of public appointments based on merit with independent assessment, openness and transparency of process. The Department is also committed to equality of opportunity and welcomes applications from all suitably qualified applicants irrespective of religious belief, gender, race, political opinion, age, disability, marital status, sexual orientation, or whether or not they have dependents. As those with disabilities and women are underrepresented, applications from these sections of the community would be particularly welcome.

item.title: Lawyer- Retail Investment Services
item.description: Lawyer- Retail Investment Services Division: Legal Department: Investments, Insurance & Redress Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £60,900 to £81,030 and London from £66,900 to £88,944 (salary offered will be based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Senior Associate, Practising Legal Your external recruitment contact is Raimonda via raimonda.stankute@fca.org.uk Your internal recruitment contact is Fizah via fizahfarouk.ibrahim@fca.org.uk Applications must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. About the FCA and team We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth and shaping the future of UK finance services. The Investments team (part of the Investments, Insurance & Redress department in the Legal Division) advises on all aspects of the conduct regulation of retail investment services. Particular projects/areas of focus include: The Consumer Duty as it relates to retail investment services as well as cross-cutting issues The Advice Guidance Boundary Review Financial promotions related to retail investment services as well as cross-cutting issues The activities of appointed representatives related to retail investment services as well as cross-cutting issues Self-invested personal pensions and funeral plans Role responsibilities Advise on the application and effect of regulatory requirements and powers to ensure firms comply with all applicable rules, legislation and law Devise and implement creative and pragmatic solutions Be fully involved in the FCA’s supervisory and policy work, including the development of policy and drafting rules and guidance in the FCA Handbook Have a high level of ownership and responsibility for your actions Supervise less experienced members of the team Skills required Minimum: Qualified lawyer (solicitor, barrister or Chartered Legal Executive or overseas equivalents): generally, a person who is at least 3 years PQE (in house, public sector or private practice) Previous experience and understanding of public law and financial services law, particularly regarding the application and interpretation of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (FSMA) and secondary legislation, FCA rules, policy making and the powers the FCA has to supervise and regulate firms Essential: Well-developed analytical skills and the ability to deliver good and clear analysis of issues Ability to learn about new or novel legal issues quickly and with enthusiasm, with the necessary oversight and support of colleagues Ability to create solutions and deliver pragmatic outcome-focused advice Ability to advise in a confident and reasoned manner and to challenge appropriately Ability to build and sustain positive relationships and good communication skills Knowledge of retail investments law is a strong advantage Benefits 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually Colleagues spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office each month (60% for Directors and Executive Directors) across our London, Leeds and Edinburgh offices. A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page . Our values and culture Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation and delivers better regulation. If you require any adjustments due to a disability or condition, your recruiter is here to help - reach out for tailored support. We welcome diverse working styles and aim to find flexible solutions that suit both the role and individual needs, including options like part-time and job sharing where applicable. Disability confident: our hiring approach We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer and therefore, people or individuals with disabilities and long-term conditions who best meet the minimum criteria for a role will go through to the next stage of the recruitment process. In cases of high application volumes we may progress applicants whose experience most closely matches the role’s key requirements. Useful information and timelines Timeline: Job advert closes: Midnight, 4th October 2026 CV Review/Shortlist: 6th October 2026 Interview including a case study: from the 13/10 moving forward Your Recruiter will discuss the process in detail with you during screening for the role, therefore, please make them aware if you are going to be unavailable for any date during this time.
