item.title: Banknote Function Manager in DEBDEN BANKNOTE OPERATIONS
item.description: Location : Loughton, Essex. About the Team The Banknote Operations team is based in Loughton, Essex and consists of six key functions which support the Notes Directorate’s key objective of having the right notes at the right place and right time and facilitating the threat assessment in support of the Bank’s anti-counterfeiting strategy: Mutilated Notes, Note Distribution, Counterfeit Analysis, Returned Note, Quality Control, Machine Testing Framework. The Banknote Function Manager is one of three managers leading daily operations across the area. Role Responsibilities The role includes: Managing operational teams and pooled resources to deliver daily and weekly targets across our functions. Driving team engagement and performance through clear objectives, coaching, and development. Select capable team members from the available resources to handle tasks as needed, collaborating with other managers to identify and address key priorities. On completion of training, acting as an Expert Witness in counterfeit-related cases, representing the Bank in court proceedings and supporting law enforcement investigations. It includes advising on matters related to banknotes and counterfeits, examining police evidence and preparing statements for court. Attendance at a UK to give evidence in person court may be required, sometimes at short notice, but this is infrequent. Depending on the court location and the case, this may also require overnight stays. Maintaining operational controls focused on security, accuracy, and efficiency. Preparing statistical data and presenting performance reports to senior managers. This is a people management role. You will be responsible for day to day management of the team and for defining roles and responsibilities. You will develop your team through sharing information effectively, coaching and communicating a clear vision to ensure that your staff are productive, engaged and motivated to deliver the area's aims. This will include setting clear goals and smart stretching objectives that are aligned to those of the team, division and directorate. You will also be responsible for managing all staff-related matters that may arise including performance, absence and sickness. Number of direct reports: Minimum one Team Leader plus matrix management of pooled resources. Role Requirements Minimum Criteria People management with ability to tackle performance issues effectively. Confidence in public speaking and ability to represent the Bank in court as an Expert Witness. Strong numerical accuracy and attention to detail. Ability to use SAP-based systems and Excel for data analysis and reporting. Essential Criteria Experience in managing operational teams and implementing work schedules. Strong stakeholder management and negotiation skills. Ability to adapt plans to meet changing operational requirements. Understanding of risk management and operational controls in high-value environments. Excellent interpersonal and communication skills (written and verbal). Ability to prepare and present technical information clearly to non-technical audiences. Desirable Criteria Experience in forensic examination of security documents or counterfeit detection. Knowledge of banknote manufacture and security features. Previous experience working with law enforcement agencies. Advanced IT skills beyond SAP and Excel. Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve. At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public. We are fully committed to having a diverse and inclusive working environment, and as such, this role is open to job shares and part time working patterns. This role is, however, an onsite role so opportunities to work from home are rare and by exception. Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme . If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application. Salary and Benefits Information This role offers a fixed starting salary of £46,350. In addition, we also offer a comprehensive benefits package as detailed below. Part time salary and benefits will be on a pro-rated basis as appropriate. Currently a non-contributory, career average pension giving you a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80th of your annual salary for every year worked. There is the option to increase your pension (to 1/65th) or decrease (to 1/105th) in exchange for salary through our flexible benefits programme each year. The Bank has the discretion to vary standard accrual rates and dial up and dial down rates at any time and to withdraw dial up and dial down options at any time. A discretionary performance award based on a current award pool. An 8% benefits allowance with the option to take as salary or purchase a wide range of flexible benefits. 26 days’ annual leave with option to buy up to 12 additional days through flexible benefits. Private medical insurance and income protection. National Security Vetting Process Employment in this role will be subject to the National Security Vetting clearance process (and typically can take between 6 to 12 weeks post offer) and the passing of additional Bank security checks in accordance with the Bank policy. Further information regarding the vetting and security clearance requirements for the role will be provided to the successful applicant, and information about how the Bank processes personal data for these purposes, is set out in the Bank's Privacy Notice . The Bank of England welcomes applications from all candidates, but as a UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) approved sponsor, we have a responsibility to comply with the Immigration Rules and guidance. As such, our ability to employ individuals who require sponsorship for immigration purposes is limited. The Bank cannot guarantee that you and / or the role you are applying for will be eligible for sponsorship and that any application made to UKVI will be successful. Eligibility will therefore be considered on a case by case basis. The Application Process Important: Please ensure that you complete the ‘work history’ section and answer ALL the application questions fully. All candidate applications are anonymised to ensure that our hiring managers will not be able to see your personal information, including your CV, when reviewing your application details at the screening stage. It’s therefore really important that you fill out the work history and application form questions, as your answers will form a critical part of the initial selection process. The assessment process will comprise of two interview stages including a presentation and will be conducted on site at our Loughton location. This role closes for applications on 13 October 2026, Please apply online, ensuring that you complete your work history and answer ALL the application questions fully and in detail as your application will not be considered if all mandatory questions are not fully completed.

item.title: Security Supervisor in Security Ops London
item.description: Location: Threadneedle Street and Moorgate, with deployment to other Bank locations where required Working arrangement: Fully site-based operational role Working pattern: Monday to Friday, eight hours per day inclusive of a one-hour break. Occasional attendance outside normal hours may be required for planned training, exercises, or significant operational needs, in accordance with contractual terms and Bank policy. Reports to: Designated Security Shift Manager Supervisory responsibility: Day-to-day supervision of a designated security cohort, currently approximately 20 personnel About the role Security Operations is responsible for protecting the Bank’s people, buildings, assets, information, and operations. Working across a complex and high-profile estate, the function contributes to the Bank’s operational resilience and its responsibilities as part of the UK’s Critical National Infrastructure. As a Security Supervisor, you will provide visible frontline leadership and oversee the safe, professional, and effective delivery of security operations. Your primary responsibility will be the day-to-day supervision of a designated Monday-to-Friday security cohort and associated public-facing, access-control, and external-interface activities. You will allocate duties, maintain operational standards, support officer welfare and development, coordinate resources and make proportionate tactical decisions within your delegated authority. To maintain operational flexibility, you may also supervise or support wider Security Operations activity across Bank locations where you are appropriately trained, competent, and authorised. This is a frontline supervisory role. Security Managers retain accountability for overall operational command, rostering, workforce planning, strategic direction, significant changes to operating arrangements and formal employee-relations decisions. Key responsibilities You will: Provide visible leadership and day-to-day supervision to in-house security personnel. Coordinate public-facing security, access control, screening, searches, vehicle, and delivery activity, guarding, and patrols. Translate management priorities into clear briefings, instructions, and operational tasking. Allocate duties, monitor post coverage, and maintain accurate information on personnel locations and operational commitments. Ensure personnel maintain high standards of vigilance, conduct, appearance, customer service, and procedural compliance. Respond to incidents, alarms, and emergencies, making timely and proportionate tactical decisions within delegated authority. Initiate approved security and emergency procedures, coordinate available resources, and maintain effective communication until responsibility transfers to a Security Manager or the emergency services. Ensure incidents, decisions, handovers, and operational activity are recorded and escalated appropriately. Address immediate concerns relating to standards, conduct or performance through instruction, feedback, and coaching, escalating serious or repeated concerns through the appropriate management arrangements. Support day-to-day attendance, sickness, welfare, and development matters within the boundaries of the role. Conduct proportionate checks of posts, equipment, records and operational delivery, supporting audits, exercises, and assurance activity. Deliver operational briefings and task-specific instruction, identify training needs, and communicate learning from incidents and exercises. Apply security controls firmly, consistently, proportionately, and respectfully. Build effective working relationships with Bank colleagues, contracted security providers, visitors, contractors, senior stakeholders, emergency services, and external security partners. Contribute frontline knowledge and operational feedback to reviews and service improvements. Operational scope Your duties may include: Access control and identity verification Perimeter, reception, and front-of-house security Vehicle access, deliveries, and screening Personal, property, vehicle, and building searches X-ray and other screening activities Static guarding and patrols Security Control Room operations Monitoring CCTV, access-control, alarm, fire, and communication systems Event and incident support Responses to security, fire, and medical emergencies Specialist or unfamiliar duties will only be undertaken where the necessary training, competence, equipment, and authority are in place. About you Minimum criteria You must be able to demonstrate: Experience supervising or leading personnel in a security or comparable operational environment. Experience responding to incidents and implementing emergency procedures. Clear verbal and written communication skills. The ability to work the stated Monday-to-Friday pattern and across Bank locations as required. Essential criteria You will also need: The ability to provide visible frontline leadership and clear operational direction. Strong situational awareness, sound judgement, and proportionate decision-making under pressure. The ability to coordinate resources, manage competing priorities and escalate shortfalls or risks promptly. Experience addressing operational standards, conduct and performance through instruction, coaching, and appropriate escalation. The ability to support attendance, welfare, and staff development within defined supervisory boundaries. Good working knowledge of access control, searches, screening, patrols, guarding, and building-security operations. Competence in relevant security technology, including CCTV, access-control, alarm, fire, communication, and screening systems. The ability to operate effectively in a Security Control Room environment, assess information, maintain accurate records, coordinate responses, and escalate incidents. A professional, customer-focused approach and the confidence to engage with a wide range of stakeholders. High standards of integrity, discretion, professionalism, and personal accountability. The flexibility to support wider Security Operations activity within the remit of the role. Desirable criteria It would be beneficial to have: Experience in Critical National Infrastructure, financial services, government, or another high-security environment. Experience supervising both in-house and contracted security personnel. Relevant security, Control Room, first-aid, incident-management, or screening qualifications. Experience supporting operational training, exercises, assurance activity, or post-incident reviews. Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve. At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public. Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme . If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application. Salary and Benefits Information We encourage flexible working, part time working and job share arrangements. Part time salary and benefits will be on a pro-rated basis as appropriate. Location London Sites - This role offers a salary of £33,600 - £37,800 In addition, we also offer a comprehensive benefits package as detailed below: Currently a non-contributory, career average pension giving you a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80th of your annual salary for every year worked. There is the option to increase your pension (to 1/65th) or decrease (to 1/105th) in exchange for salary through our flexible benefits programme each year. The Bank has the discretion to vary standard accrual rates and dial up and dial down rates at any time and to withdraw dial up and dial down options at any time. A discretionary performance award based on a current award pool. An 8% benefits allowance with the option to take as salary or purchase a wide range of flexible benefits. 26 days’ annual leave with option to buy up to 12 additional days through flexible benefits. Private medical insurance and income protection. item.title: Financial Crime Data Analyst
item.description: Job Title: Financial Crime Data Analyst Division: Supervision, Policy & Competition (SPC) Department: Financial Crime Markets (FCMI) Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £43,100 to £48,000 and London £47,300 to £53,000 (salary offered will be based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Associate – Level 8 – Regulatory Your external recruitment contact is Steve Christopher via steve.christopher@fca.org.uk . Your internal recruitment contact is Isabelle Groves via isabelle.groves@fca.org.uk . Applications must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. About the FCA and team We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth and shaping the future of financial services in the UK. SPC oversees firms and individuals (supervision), creates and reviews the rules by which they operate (policy) and identifies and remedies ineffective competition in markets (competition. The Financial Crime Market Intervention department, within the Specialist Directorate, provides specialist expertise to help reduce the risk that regulated businesses are used for financial crime. The department includes four Financial Crime Specialist Supervision teams, a Sanctions Supervision Team, a Fraud Supervision Team and a Risk, Data and Strategy Team. Working with colleagues across the FCA and external partners, it focuses on money laundering, financial sanctions, fraud, bribery and corruption. This role sits in the Risk, Data and Strategy Team. Role responsibilities Help shape innovative data-led approaches that enhance the FCA’s ability to prevent and detect financial crime, protecting consumers and markets across the UK Turn complex data into clear, actionable insights that support supervisory decisions and drive meaningful regulatory outcomes Collaborate with colleagues across Data and Supervision to deliver impactful projects that enhance the FCA’s financial crime capabilities Develop specialist skills in data analytics within a high-profile regulatory environment, building skills and experience that can help protect millions of consumers Skills required Minimum: Prior experience using Excel, SQL, or another data analytics tool to interrogate and manipulate data Prior experience analysing data to answer defined questions and draw practical conclusions Prior experience presenting analysis clearly in written, visual, or verbal formats Essential: Effective communication skills, with the ability to explain data analysis and insights clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences Ability to deliver high-quality work to tight deadlines, using initiative and sound judgement Well-developed stakeholder management skills, with the ability to build effective relationships, provide constructive challenge and confidently engage with senior stakeholders Ability to prioritise competing demands and manage multiple pieces of work with minimal supervision A collaborative and forward-thinking approach, demonstrating curiosity, innovation and a positive attitude to problem-solving Confidence in making informed judgements, taking timely decisions and learning from experience to continuously improve outcomes Experience creating data visualisation dashboards (e.g. Tableau), analytical programming languages (e.g. Python, R or advanced SQL) and knowledge of financial services, regulation, financial crime, or supervisory data is desirable Benefits 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays Colleagues spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office each month (60% for Directors and Executive Directors) across our London, Leeds and Edinburgh offices Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page . Our values and culture Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation and delivers better regulation. If you require any adjustments due to a disability or condition, your recruiter is here to help - reach out for tailored support. We welcome diverse working styles and aim to find flexible solutions that suit both the role and individual needs, including options like part-time and job sharing where applicable. Disability confident: our hiring approach We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer and therefore, people or individuals with disabilities and long-term conditions who best meet the minimum criteria for a role will go through to the next stage of the recruitment process. In cases of high application volumes we may progress applicants whose experience most closely matches the role’s key requirements. Useful information and timelines Timeline: Job advert close: 30th September 2026 at Midnight CV Review/Shortlist: 2nd - 6th October 2026 Interviews w/c 19th October 2026 Your Recruiter will discuss the process in detail with you during screening for the role, therefore, please make them aware if you are going to be unavailable for any date during this time .

item.title: HR Systems Associate
item.description: Job title: HR Systems Associate Division: Operations Department: Human Resources Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £39,100 to £48,800 and London from £41,600 to £51,900 (salary offered will be based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Corporate, L8 – Associate Your external recruitment contact is Raimonda via raimonda.stankute@fca.org.uk Your internal recruitment contact is Lauren via lauren.mchale@fca.org.uk Applications must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. About the FCA and team We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth and shaping the future of UK finance services. We are transforming to become a data-led regulator that identifies and runs towards future problems while pursuing the opportunities ahead. As part of this journey, our People function is evolving to ensure our systems, processes and data support the FCA to be at its best. Reliable people data relies on well-managed HR technology, and our HR Systems Associate plays an important role in supporting and maintaining our HR systems. Working as part of the HR Analytics & Systems team, this role provides day-to-day support for Workday and associated HR technologies. You will help ensure the smooth operation of HR processes, support colleagues across HR and the wider organisation, investigate system issues, maintain data quality and contribute to system improvements. You will also have the opportunity to develop your Workday skills through hands-on involvement in configuration activities, testing, data management and integrations support, including Enterprise Interface Builder (EIB) data loads. This role is ideal for someone with some experience of HR systems who enjoys problem-solving, working with data and delivering a positive user experience. Role responsibilities Provide day-to-day administration and user support for Workday and other HR systems, investigating queries, resolving issues and supporting the smooth delivery of HR processes Support core HR processes within Workday, ensuring transactions are completed accurately and in accordance with agreed procedures Carry out routine system administration and maintenance activities, including updates to reference data, notifications, system settings, approved configuration changes and maintenance of system documentation and guidance materials Support data quality and governance activities through audits, validation checks, reporting, data corrections and ongoing monitoring Prepare, validate and process Workday EIB data loads, and support integrations and data transfer activities by monitoring interfaces, investigating errors and working with colleagues and suppliers to resolve issues Support Workday releases, enhancements and projects through testing, user acceptance testing (UAT), documentation updates and post-release activities Collaborate with HR, Payroll, IT and wider stakeholders to understand requirements, support effective business processes and deliver a positive user experience Contribute to continuous improvement by identifying opportunities to enhance system functionality, data quality, user experience and operational processes Skills required Minimum: Proven experience using, supporting or administering Workday or another HR system in an operational environment Demonstrable experience of working with core HR processes across the employee lifecycle, using HR systems to support effective process controls and maintain accurate employee data undefined Essential: Experience supporting HR system users, providing guidance on system processes and transactions and delivering a positive user experience Experience with HR system administration, maintenance, testing and configuration activities, including updates to reference data, notifications, business processes or other system settings Experience working with HR data, including data validation, data quality management, reporting, audits, updates and governance activities Experience preparing, validating or processing data loads, EIBs, integrations or related data transfer processes within Workday or similar systems Solid analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify, investigate and resolve system and data issues in a structured manner Effective written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences and build effective relationships across teams Well-organised and self-motivated, with the ability to prioritise competing workloads, manage multiple tasks and demonstrate a continuous improvement mindset Benefits 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually Colleagues spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office each month (60% for Directors and Executive Directors) across our London, Leeds and Edinburgh offices. A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page . Our values and culture Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation and delivers better regulation. If you require any adjustments due to a disability or condition, your recruiter is here to help - reach out for tailored support. We welcome diverse working styles and aim to find flexible solutions that suit both the role and individual needs, including options like part-time and job sharing where applicable.
